scores.quote: We are mitigating this through calibrated price increases... we have already announced price increases of 6% to 8% for this current quarter.

scores.rationale: Entry barriers are high — INR 5,800 cr to add one plant's capacity — and pricing behaviour is rational, with cost inflation being passed through rather than absorbed in a discount war, though Europe's structurally weak market forced capacity closure.
scores.quote: the Board of Directors in the recent meeting approved a INR 5,800 crores capex for our AP plant

scores.rationale: No weak competitors are identified as donating share; if anything the flow ran the other way in exports and PCR OEM during Q1, and Q4 gains are attributed to market demand rather than to rivals losing.
scores.quote: Exports were impacted by events through the year. So the overseas markets were muted.

scores.rationale: This is the opposite of an ignored niche — a large listed tyre maker in a heavily analyst-covered sector that has just bought the most visible sponsorship property in India.
scores.quote: our logo is now prominently featured on the official Team India jersey

scores.rationale: There is real brand-building (dual-brand strategy, Vredestein at record volumes, cricket sponsorship) but no evident image-driven pricing power — price rises only follow raw-material inflation and consolidated EBITDA margin is a modest 14.6%.
scores.quote: Our dual brand strategy is paying off with our premium brand Vredestein continuing to make rapid strides and once again recording highest ever volumes

scores.rationale: Premium OEMs buying on validated performance rather than price is real assurance-type demand, evidenced by repeat German OEM model wins and consistent podium finishes in independent European tests.
scores.quote: we are continuing to win podium positions in Europe at independent test results

scores.rationale: Deliberate investment in access and customer intimacy — added dealer distribution off the sponsorship, a new B2B e-commerce platform in Europe, and 35 healthcare centres plus a telemedicine app serving the trucking community.
scores.quote: we have recently inaugurated our 35th Healthcare Centre in Rajasthan, enhancing healthcare access for the trucking community

scores.rationale: The benefit mix is well matched to both customer sets — mass-retail emotional branding via cricket for replacement buyers, and technical validation plus model approvals for OEM/fleet corporate customers.
scores.quote: Cricket is India's strongest culture and sporting platform with unmatched reach and emotional connection

scores.rationale: R&D is competent and productive (UHP mix to 52%, Aspire 5 launch, AI in manufacturing and service) but the calls show approvals won alongside global rivals rather than a proprietary, multi-product technology edge.
scores.quote: the UHP mix for the quarter increased to 52%, compared to the 48% for the same quarter last year

scores.rationale: Nothing in the business as described is self-reinforcing with scale — tyres are sold through dealers and OEMs with no two-sided network dynamic anywhere in the four calls.

Distribution is a genuine strength being actively widened — sponsorship-driven dealer additions in India, a truck-driver service network, and a new European B2B platform — though it is not a reach rivals like MRF cannot match.
scores.quote: driving unparalleled brand reach and visibility and adding distribution... has boosted dealer morale and is already translating into positive business outcomes

scores.rationale: Branch network grew 301→339 with 39 added in FY26 and 60-70 planned for FY27 plus doubled IT spend, yet opex/AUM held at 2.7-2.8% while ROE stayed above 20% — growth investment funded without diluting incremental returns.
scores.quote: we have planned 40 branch openings, most of which are already operational. For the next financial year, we plan to accelerate expansion to 60 to 70 branches

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend in any of the four calls; sourcing is discussed only as branch, digital referral and connector channels.
As a housing financier there is no R&D line; technology spend (ZIVA LOS, lead-management app) is discussed as process infrastructure, not as an R&D engine producing new products.
No acquisitions, no inorganic transactions and no M&A intent mentioned across the last four calls.
A modest, consistent dividend of INR4.50 was declared for FY26 while capital is retained to fund 20%+ AUM growth — coherent for a compounding lender, but there is no buyback discipline to judge.
scores.quote: we have declared a dividend of INR4.50 including the dividend of INR2.50 that was declared in the Board meeting 6th May 2026

scores.rationale: Lending is inherently balance-sheet-heavy rather than asset-light — growth consumes equity — though the returns earned on those assets are exceptional at 8.2% ROA and 21.2% ROE with best-in-class 2.8% opex/AUM.
scores.quote: translating into an ROA and ROE of 8.2% and 21.2% amongst the highest in the industry

scores.rationale: AUM compounded 21-24% y-o-y to INR13,107 crores with customers up 20%, well above system growth in a fragmented affordable-housing market where Aptus is still small, leaving long runway.
scores.quote: AUM grew by 21% year-on-year to INR13,107 crores

scores.rationale: Contiguous entry into Maharashtra and Odisha has progressed from a INR67 crore book to 15 branches within the year with management calling early experience encouraging, but the base is still trivial versus a INR13,107 crore book.
scores.quote: In Maharashtra and Odisha, our loan book has crossed ■67 crores. The initial experience in these states have been good.

scores.rationale: Growth is volume- and ticket-size-led while pricing is being actively cut — 50-75bps off incremental home loans — so price is a headwind rather than a driver, with only ATS/mix upgrade working in the company's favour.
scores.quote: we have reduced the interest rate by 50 to 75 basis points on incremental home loan disbursements

scores.rationale: The company is riding a favourable funding-rate cycle, with cost of funds falling from 8.62% to 8.1% and spreads widening to 9%, though much of the benefit is already banked and partly passed through to borrowers.
scores.quote: Our spread improved to 9%, driven by decline in cost of funds to 8.1%

scores.rationale: Management explicitly frames affordable housing for self-employed customers in Tier 3/4 towns as a structurally expanding end market, which is consistent with four quarters of 20%+ AUM growth through a soft disbursement patch.
scores.quote: the affordable housing segment we operate in remains structurally robust and has strong potential for growth

scores.rationale: Purely organic growth with no M&A, a deliberate decision to forgo roughly INR283 crores of sub-INR7 lakh disbursements for quality, INR2,057 crores of liquidity and a rating upgrade to CARE AA evidence prudent stewardship.
scores.quote: we discontinued sanctions below 7 lakhs. While this decision led to temporary moderation in disbursements in Q1 and Q2, we rebounded strongly in Q4

scores.rationale: A consistently repeated INR25,000 crore AUM goal by FY28-29 is being pursued through a self-inflicted disbursement slowdown, and management held the sub-INR7 lakh exit through two weak quarters until Q4 delivered a record INR1,242 crores.
scores.quote: Aligned with our vision of scaling our AUM to ■25,000 crores by FY28-29

scores.rationale: Calls are delivered in plain operating detail by the same founder-chairman/MD team with no promotional flourish or celebrity positioning, though the stock is actively covered by Citi, Yes Securities and Dolat.
scores.quote: we are steadily investing in branch expansion, digital capabilities and strengthening the talent pool, particularly in the middle management level

scores.rationale: There is real investment in the middle-management pipeline and a structured collections hierarchy, but Tamil Nadu attrition is admitted to be high with rivals poaching staff, and the 5-year history shows both chairmen, an MD and two CFOs exiting.
scores.quote: in Tamil Nadu, the attrition is slightly high... if anybody wants to open a branch in Tamil Nadu, the first thing they do is to take people from us

scores.rationale: Management volunteered the disbursement dip and its causes, quantified the sub-INR7 lakh drag precisely (INR283 crores, INR163 crores in Q4), disclosed the write-off policy change to 500 days and the INR3.85 crore labour-code hit, and flagged an SME NPA uptick unprompted.
scores.quote: we have now decided to go for 100% technical write-off of outstanding beyond 500 days. Earlier, we were partly following a practice of 100% write-off beyond 2 years.

scores.rationale: Headline 26% PAT growth and 20%+ ROE invite a halo, but stripped back, FY26 disbursements grew only 11%, GNPA drifted from 1.19% to 1.52% and 30+ DPD sits at 6.21% — earnings were carried by spread expansion from falling funding costs as much as by operating skill.
scores.quote: We finished FY '26 with the GNPA 1.52% as against 1.19% in FY '25

scores.rationale: Nothing in the calls suggests a monopoly-like hold on the customer's mind; management concedes competition is higher in its core Tamil Nadu market and peers enter its towns freely.
scores.quote: in Tamil Nadu, the competition is slightly higher

scores.rationale: Switching costs appear weak — the company had to cut incremental home-loan rates by 50-75bps to defend and win customers — with the only real friction being physical branch proximity in Tier 3/4 towns.
scores.quote: optimizing lending rates across segments in line with our strategy to onboard higher quality customers and aid growth further

scores.rationale: The affordable-housing/LAP segment described is fragmented with many players and easy entry into Aptus's own towns, so this is not a stable oligopoly and borrowers can shop for rate.
scores.quote: if anybody wants to open a branch in Tamil Nadu, the first thing they do is to take people from us

scores.rationale: Entry barriers are low — a competitor can open a branch simply by hiring away Aptus staff — and pricing is drifting downward with incremental rate cuts rather than holding firm.
scores.quote: the first thing they do is to take people from us

scores.rationale: Peers in MFI and small-ticket MSME lending are visibly stressed while Aptus's 40% LTV book is not, giving it a pool of weakening competitors to take share from.
scores.quote: there are like a lot many players highlighting stress on the MSME side, on the self-employed side... we are not seeing that kind of pressure

scores.rationale: The Tier 3/4 self-employed niche is genuinely unglamorous, but the company is listed, institutionally held and covered by Citi, Yes Securities and Dolat, so it is hardly ignored by capital.
scores.quote: during the year, as you know, we broadened our shareholder base and further diversified institutional shareholding

scores.rationale: Credit is a commodity here with no image- or taste-driven pricing power; high yields reflect risk pricing on informal-income borrowers and are being cut where competition bites.
scores.quote: we have reduced the interest rate by 50 to 75 basis points on incremental home loan disbursements

scores.rationale: Underserved self-employed borrowers do buy certainty of sanction from a lender that will underwrite them, but the need to optimize lending rates shows price is not secondary for these customers.
scores.quote: serving self-employed customers through a wide suite of housing and business loan products with a deeper presence in Tier 3 and Tier 4 towns

scores.rationale: A 339-branch physical network in Tier 3/4 towns is paired with unusually direct customer intimacy — the sourcing branch manager and sales officer own collections for the first 12 EMIs — plus 21% digital-referral sourcing.
scores.quote: up to 12 EMIs, it will be the responsibility of the branch team, branch manager and the sales officer who generated the proposal to be totally in charge of the first 12 months collection

scores.rationale: The customer is retail self-employed, and the benefit offered is correctly matched to that — access, proximity and high-touch servicing at 40% LTV rather than corporate TCO arguments — though it is convenience rather than intangible brand pull.
scores.quote: the LTV for our loans are only 40%, which means the equity of the customer in the property in which they live is much more

scores.rationale: Technology (ZIVA LOS, mobile-first lead management, doubled IT spend) is a credible efficiency enabler holding opex at 2.7%, but it is table-stakes infrastructure rather than a defensible multi-product tech edge.
scores.quote: Our new loan origination system, what we call ZIVA has gradually stabilized across the branches

scores.rationale: The business has no self-reinforcing two-sided network; the closest analogue, the connector and construction-ecosystem referral channel, is described by management as still nascent.
scores.quote: we have expanded our connector partnership across branches. While this is still at a nascent stage

scores.rationale: 339 branches embedded in Tier 3/4 towns serving 1.65 lakh+ customers, with collections and legal recovery layered by branch, cluster and state, is a physical reach and service depth that matters most in a market where on-ground collection is the business.
scores.quote: Branch networks grew by 339 branches as of 31st March, adding 39 branches in FY '26

scores.rationale: INR348 crores of growth capex in 9M FY26 directed at garmenting/vertical expansion with ROCE improving 150bps to 16% (19% adjusted for CWIP), and management explicitly refuses low-return fabric capacity additions.
scores.quote: The company has spent about INR348 crores in various growth capex projects in the first 9 months of FY '26

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend in either call — Arvind's B2B model makes it largely irrelevant, but there is no evidence to score.
No R&D spend, pipeline, or efficiency metric disclosed; only passing references to 'innovation-based capex' which is too thin to judge.
scores.quote: We are only investing in innovation -based or dif ferentiation -based capex

scores.rationale: Dalco-GFT is a technology-adjacent bolt-on into needle-punch nonwovens Arvind already runs, bought at 7.75x EBITDA from an already-strong asset (17% margin, 40% pre-deal ROC) with founders rolling 39% equity and the deal EPS/margin accretive — though at $136m debt-funded it is not a small deal.
scores.quote: acquired 61% stake in the company at a valuation of 7.75x of calendar year 2025 reported EBITDA... both margin accretive and EPS accretive

scores.rationale: Neither call mentions dividends, buybacks, or any distribution policy.
The core is capital-heavy spinning/weaving/garmenting requiring continuous capex with ROCE only 16% (19% adjusted), and the acquired US asset also needs $5m/yr of line capex to sustain growth.
scores.quote: Return on capital during the same period improved by 150 basis points to reach 16%

scores.rationale: Sub-20% verticalization, an underrepresented EU/UK position about to be opened by FTAs, and a young geotextiles segment at Dalco give clear runway plus evidence of capture (denim volumes +16%, garments +11%).
scores.quote: we are sub -20% verticalization or just about approaching 20% now

scores.rationale: Concrete execution on geography: sales/marketing teams reallocated and hiring ahead of UK/EU FTA implementation, Bangladesh dependence deliberately reduced, and a US manufacturing footprint acquired to sit close to consumption.
scores.quote: we are reallocating a lot of internal marketing resources and sales resources to focus on these geographies

scores.rationale: Mix genuinely improved (garmenting realisation up on product mix), but realisations are otherwise flat, denim growth is explicitly volume/capacity-led, and the company is conceding ~INR25 crores/quarter of tariff discounts — pricing power is not the driver.
scores.quote: if you look at realization, it is reasonably flat... if we are able to maintain this level of growth, it will be on volume

scores.rationale: Some upturn triggers exist (UK/EU FTAs pending implementation, US infrastructure bill lifting geotextiles), but denim is already at 100% capacity utilisation, so the company is not positioned near a cycle bottom.
scores.quote: For the first time in a long time, we have reached absolute full capacity utilization

scores.rationale: The Advanced Materials leg addresses a $2.5bn TAM with a sustained 18-20% growth aspiration across defence, composites and filtration, though the textile majority is a mature end market.
scores.quote: our growth aspiration for the Advanced Materials division remains at over 20% on a CAGR basis

scores.rationale: Net debt held flat year-to-date, AAML rated AA (a notch above parent), refusal to add fabric capacity where returns are poor, and the one acquisition kept within existing covenants.
scores.quote: Our consolidated net debt remains stable and broadly in line with March 2025 levels

scores.rationale: Management frames capital allocation on a decade view — a phased garmenting category roadmap and buying rather than building a capability that would take ten years organically.
scores.quote: if we had to start this from scratch, it would take us better part of a decade to achieve any scale

scores.rationale: Calls are largely operational and detail-heavy, but management does lead with self-promotional ESG league-table rankings, so the evidence is neutral.
scores.quote: which puts us sixth in the world out of 176 participants ranked, and it puts us ahead of 97% of the participants

scores.rationale: Deliberate team-building — hiring and reallocating staff for new FTA geographies, retaining the entire acquired management with re-cut long-term performance incentives and staggered 2/4-year equity rollover.
scores.quote: we've just redone the entire sort of performance-linked long-term incentives of the entire management team

scores.rationale: Management quantifies its own headwinds (INR25 crores/quarter tariff discounts), warns against extrapolating a strong AMD quarter driven by chunky defence orders, and names Bangladesh instability as a risk rather than an opportunity.
scores.quote: it's good to, in our mind, think that it will be around 18% to 20% if you look a few quarters on average... some quarters will be below that

scores.rationale: Results are separable from skill because management itself attributes part of the quarter to favourable currency and one-off orders, leaving the underlying 12% EBITDA margin and 16% ROCE as the honest baseline.
scores.quote: macroeconom ic conditions of the dollar, et c., have been favorable

scores.rationale: The acquired US business is sole-sourced on ~85% of its automotive products and specced into Tier-1 platforms, a monopoly-like position at the customer, though this covers only the AMD leg.
scores.quote: almost 85% or maybe slightly higher than that even as sole sourced by the customer from only the company

scores.rationale: Regional monopoly economics are explicit — freight limits the serviceable radius to 500-700 miles — and automotive spec-in creates real switching costs, but the fabric business has none of this.
scores.quote: The radius of many of these products is not beyond 500 to 700 miles because then the transportation costs start to add up

scores.rationale: The core fabric market has abundant global capacity and interchangeable suppliers, and even in nonwovens management concedes larger competitors exist in geotextiles — customers hold the negotiating power.
scores.quote: There is a hug e amount of capacity available in the country and in the world

scores.rationale: Pricing is openly irrational at the customer's initiative — brands run online reverse auctions on new products and extracted tariff-related discounts that Arvind had to absorb.
scores.quote: there is an online bidding process that brands have resorted to... then you try and discover the lowest priced product

scores.rationale: Bangladesh's instability and yarn disruption plus customers' explicit desire to de-risk from it create a donor pool India and Arvind can take from, alongside larger but slower incumbents in US geotextiles.
scores.quote: All customers are worried about overdependence on Bangladesh... India suddenly starts looking much more attractive

scores.rationale: Arvind is a widely covered listed textile major with multiple sell-side analysts on the call, though the needle-punch nonwoven niche it is buying into is genuinely under-followed.
No image- or taste-based pricing power: the company absorbs tariff discounts, sees flat realisations, and runs consolidated EBITDA margins of just 12%, its 'first milestone'.
scores.quote: EBITDA for the same period stood at INR286 crores, up 15%, achieved its first milestone of crossing 12% in terms of margin

scores.rationale: Customers buy reliability — compliance governs outsourcing decisions, and the acquired business wins on top-quartile delivery and performance track record rather than price alone.
scores.quote: Our performance will be top quartile in terms of delivery, price and innovation, all 3

scores.rationale: Convenience is the stated selling proposition — a vertical full-package offering customers prefer over fabric, backed by manufacturing sited next to consumption and reinforced sales teams.
scores.quote: all the customers want a vertical offering rather than selling fabric

scores.rationale: Purely corporate customers (brands, Tier-1 auto suppliers) and the benefit stack matches — reliability, compliance and sole-source spec-in lock-in rather than consumer intangibles.
scores.quote: They are present with the 6 largest Tier 1 in the country that supply all the automotive OEMs

scores.rationale: A genuine but narrow platform edge: needle-punch nonwoven know-how transferable between Indian filtration and US automotive/geotextiles with cross-market product portability, though no R&D intensity is disclosed and textiles carry no tech edge.
scores.quote: it's a simple manufacturing platform that is creating a lot of innovative products. That's a rare combination

scores.rationale: Nothing in either call describes a two-sided or self-reinforcing network; growth is driven by capacity addition and customer-by-customer selling.

Distribution strength is real in AMD — deep relationships across all six major Tier-1s with 88% exclusive supplier access and proximity manufacturing — but is a work-in-progress in apparel where teams are still being built for EU/UK.
scores.quote: existing access to customers of around 75 with exclusive access to 88% of its supplier base

scores.rationale: Capex is clearly growth-oriented — over 1.4 lakh net sq ft of new retail space added in FY26 plus D2C/tech build-out — and incremental returns are visibly rising with ROCE at a multiyear high of 23%+.
scores.quote: We added more than 1.4 lakh net square feet of retail space... ROCE at 23% plus is a multiyear high

scores.rationale: A&P was deliberately stepped up (+20bps in Q2 FY26, ~+50bps in Q1 FY27) and is traceable to sales outcomes such as U.S. Polo's 20–25% growth, though the brands are licensed rather than owned so equity build accrues only partly to AFL.
scores.quote: we have consciously increased our investment in marketing by approximately 50 basis points year-on-year

scores.rationale: No R&D spend, pipeline, or efficiency disclosure in any of the four calls; product 'innovation' references are merchandising, not R&D.
The only deal is a small, simple bolt-on — buying back Flipkart's 31.25% stake in the already-owned Flying Machine JV — and the brand subsequently posted double-digit retail LTL and 70% B2C growth.
scores.quote: During this quarter, we acquired Flipkart stake in Flying Machine

scores.rationale: Buybacks, dividends and distribution policy are never mentioned across the four calls.
Asset-light leased-store and D2C model with stable working capital and record inventory freshness delivering 23%+ ROCE, but the 'moat' rests on licensed brands rather than owned IP.
scores.quote: working capital has been well controlled... ROCE at a new high

scores.rationale: Consistent 11–15.5% revenue growth with 8–11.6% retail LTL in a self-described 'stable' (not booming) demand environment implies share capture, and the fragmented Indian apparel market leaves ample runway.
scores.quote: we recorded a 15.5% revenue growth... The demand environment remains stable

scores.rationale: Expansion is store-count density within India only; the licensed brand portfolio (USPA, Tommy, CK) is territory-restricted so no international expansion is contemplated or discussed.
scores.quote: Sourcing remains predominantly India-based

scores.rationale: Margin gains come from mix (D2C share to 62%, premiumization, adjacencies at 24%) and lower discounting rather than headline price hikes, with pricing action only contemplated defensively against input inflation.
scores.quote: Full price sell-through is up and discounting is down, resulting in a gross margin improvement of approximately 90 basis points

scores.rationale: Discretionary apparel is being lifted off a soft base by GST 2.0, income tax and rate cuts, with management explicitly flagging an improving demand cycle ahead — though West Asia-led inflation is a stated offsetting risk.
scores.quote: Government measures around GST, interest rates, and income tax have supported demand

scores.rationale: End market benefits from durable formalization/premiumization of Indian branded apparel and a structural online shift, evidenced by 38–50% sustained online B2C growth and 20%+ growth in adjacent categories.
scores.quote: Online B2C grew over 38%, taking its share of revenue to 18% from 15% a year ago

scores.rationale: Consistent organic 'profitable growth' mantra with ROCE as the stated North Star, stable working capital, and only a tiny bolt-on stake buyback rather than large M&A.
scores.quote: We continue to stay focused on our mantra of profitable growth, resulting in further improvement in return on capital employed

scores.rationale: A coherent multi-year agenda — 5 strategic pillars, D2C share target of 65%, Flying Machine repositioning and dotcom launches — is being executed on schedule quarter after quarter.
scores.quote: we will continue to double down on our D2C journey with a vision to take the share of D2C to 65%

scores.rationale: Calls are metric-dense and free of celebrity posturing, but there is no affirmative evidence of a deliberately low-profile posture and the company is actively courting brand visibility and analyst coverage.
scores.quote: increasing brand visibility through marquee advertising campaigns

scores.rationale: Management cites investment in people, a completed reorganization into accountable business units, and an orderly CEO handover, though the rapid MD turnover in the history table tempers confidence in the pipeline.
scores.quote: The seamless transition to new leadership has ensured continued growth momentum

scores.rationale: Negatives are disclosed reasonably plainly — Arrow subdued, PVH hit by GST and sourcing disruption, PAT decline explained by lower other income, wage-code charge called out — though setbacks are quickly framed as 'transitory'.
scores.quote: Arrow was subdued due to a onetime model change and a weak wedding calendar. Both are timing-related and not structural.

scores.rationale: Strong headline PAT growth flatters off a weak base (a INR93 crore loss in Q4 FY25) and the brand pull is licensed rather than built, so results should not be read purely as management skill despite genuinely consistent LTL and margin delivery.
scores.quote: PAT came in at INR47 crores versus a loss of INR93 crores in Q4 last year

scores.rationale: U.S. Polo holds a strong mindshare position in Indian casual menswear, but it is a licensed brand in a crowded category with no aftermarket or services lock-in.
scores.quote: USPA led the pack, delivering its highest-ever growth this quarter

scores.rationale: Apparel carries essentially zero switching costs — consumers can move brands garment to garment — and nothing in the calls suggests regional exclusivity or captive demand.
Indian branded apparel is highly fragmented, and AFL's own dependence on wholesale, MBO, department stores and marketplace platforms leaves the end customer with full negotiating latitude.
scores.quote: Wholesale and department stores delivered strong double-digit secondary sales growth

scores.rationale: Barriers are low and the industry remains discount-driven — the company entered EOSS a week early and reported higher overall discounting in Q3 — even though AFL is itself pushing toward full-price selling.
scores.quote: we entered EOSS a week earlier than usual. Overall discount was higher

scores.rationale: Growth well above a flat market, plus a deliberate retreat from online B2B and continued double-digit secondary sales, points to share being taken from weaker unorganized and regional players.
scores.quote: Both MBO and department store secondary sales have also witnessed a very strong double-digit growth

scores.rationale: This is a widely covered listed consumer name with consumer-facing brands and multiple sell-side analysts on every call — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: line of Avinash K from Motilal Oswal Financial Services Limited

scores.rationale: Gross margin of 56.7% and rising, with premiumization and full-price sell-through improving, indicates real image-driven pricing power in the portfolio.
scores.quote: gross margin improvement of approximately 90 basis points to 56.7%

scores.rationale: Fashion apparel is bought on taste and trend, not on certainty or reliability; the calls' own framing is trend, positioning and expression rather than dependability.
scores.quote: more tailored to an on-trend expression with denim at its core

scores.rationale: D2C is now 62% of sales via own stores, marketplaces and brand dotcoms/apps, giving direct ownership of the customer relationship and broad accessibility.
scores.quote: We are building our business around channels where we own the customer relationship

scores.rationale: The customer base is retail consumers and the benefit offered is correctly intangible/brand-led — premiumization, advertising and store experience — matching benefit type to customer.
scores.quote: driving premiumization, and that is another trend that has worked extremely well for U.S. Polo

scores.rationale: Technology is a back-office efficiency and analytics project at an admittedly early stage, not a differentiated multi-product tech edge.
scores.quote: Our investments in analytics technology and AI are starting to bear very early results

scores.rationale: No two-sided network exists in the business model; the only community reference is an aspirational Gen Z brand community for Flying Machine, which is marketing rather than a network effect.
scores.quote: building relevance, community and cultural momentum with our Gen Z consumers

scores.rationale: AFL commands a genuinely broad multi-channel reach — EBOs, MBOs, department stores, marketplaces and owned online — expanding at 1.4 lakh sq ft a year, which smaller rivals cannot replicate, though larger apparel groups can.
scores.quote: We added more than 1.4 lakh net square feet of retail space

scores.rationale: Heavy and rising growth capex — a ~Rs.80 crore bridge, three ports, 300km of roads, a 20,000 tpd washing plant, port expansion from 15 to 20 mt and Rs.150 crore of India capex — with volumes and EBITDA rising, but per-tonne economics remain thin (USD 8.9/mt) so incremental ROIC is unproven.
scores.quote: we are doing the expansion in our port facilities which will be expected to be ready by end of this year and we will be able to increase our volume from 15 million tons to 20 million tons

scores.rationale: No mention of advertising or promotional spend in any of the four calls.
Product development is an explicit focus in the India business with a widening value-added basket, but no R&D spend or efficiency metric is disclosed.
scores.quote: A key area of focus for us is the development and commercialization of new products across our India business

scores.rationale: No acquisitions were discussed in the window; expansion is organic and via contracting partnerships, not deals.
No dividend, buyback or distribution policy is discussed in any of the four calls.

The business is structurally asset-heavy — self-built ports, mining roads, bridges, washing and beneficiation plants funded over eight to nine years of continuous investment — the opposite of asset-light.
scores.quote: we could see almost you can say the period of eight to nine years, we are continuously investing in this territory

scores.rationale: Ashapura is a small player in a Guinea market where Chinese firms do ~90% of the business, and it doubled exports from 3.5 mt to 8 mt in FY26 against a ~200 mt national export base — clear runway plus demonstrated capture.
scores.quote: we have ended almost the export of 8 million tons of bauxite against 3.5 million tons in the previous year

scores.rationale: The Guinea entry since 2016 has been executed with real infrastructure and is now producing volume, and India products reach 80+ countries — credible and well-executed, though it is commodity rather than brand-led.
scores.quote: Ashapura is only one company who have now sustainable a kind of standing in Guinea

scores.rationale: Growth is entirely volume-led while realisations fell — a ~3% bauxite price correction, an admitted price concern, and an India mix shift toward lower-margin products.
scores.quote: profitability was affected by higher input costs and changes in product mix, with a higher proportion of lower-margin products contributing to overall sales

scores.rationale: Management places bauxite pricing near a trough with identifiable upturn triggers — price stabilisation, LME aluminium at $3,600 heading to $4,000, and a proposed Guinean export quota that would tighten supply.
scores.quote: the Guinea government is planning to implement the bauxite quota systems... that will definitely have a positive impact on Ashapura

scores.rationale: Guinea is described as the only commercially viable long-term bauxite supplier to the world with growing aluminium consumption, though near-term alumina oversupply and geopolitical disturbance temper the secular story.
scores.quote: you won't see any other country in the world who can replace Guinea now or in next 10 years

scores.rationale: Growth is organic with no M&A and counter-cyclical multi-year investment in Guinea, but management itself frames the strategy as high-risk given limited resources, and leverage is never addressed.
scores.quote: we had very limited resources, and we had like unlimited ambitions, so it is a very high risk, high reward kind of a territory

scores.rationale: An 11-year Guinea build-out — three ports, 300km of heavy-haul roads, a 100-metre bridge — pursued independently in a market dominated by Chinese majors is strong evidence of long-term tenacity.
scores.quote: The journey was a long journey for last 11 years and now we have fairly established in Guinea

scores.rationale: The company held its maiden earnings call only in September 2025 after four decades of operations, and the tone is operational rather than promotional.
scores.quote: this earning call which is really a maiden call for Ashapura Group

scores.rationale: Leadership is promoter-family based with succession running from Chetan Shah to Manan Shah, and no systematic talent development or internal pipeline is described beyond generic team appreciation.
scores.quote: Thank you, Dad. Coming to our India business

scores.rationale: Management openly conceded a shortfall in Q3 with specific causes, admitted the bauxite price worry as its own, and voluntarily flagged the labour-code exceptional item and India margin pressure.
scores.quote: I agree that our quarterly results are par with our previous quarter, but certainly it is slightly below the expectations

scores.rationale: The 105% topline surge is heavily attributable to bauxite volumes and commodity conditions rather than demonstrable per-unit skill — EBITDA per tonne actually slipped to USD 8.9 — so results should not be read as proof of managerial edge.
scores.quote: EBITDA per metric ton of Guinea bauxite has dropped very slightly. It was USD 8.9 per metric ton compared to USD 9.3 per metric ton in Quarter 1

scores.rationale: Leading positions in Indian bentonite, bleaching clay and kaolin plus the first propant plant in India give a near-monopoly standing in narrow domestic mineral niches, though not in bauxite.
scores.quote: today Ashapura is the largest bentonite producer in India and third largest in the world

scores.rationale: The India business enjoys a locational quasi-monopoly with captive mines, plant and seaport inside a 100km radius plus seven new bentonite leases, but there is no evidence of customer switching costs.
scores.quote: The proximity between the mines to the plant to the main seaport is all in 100 kilometer radius which is a very rare kind of a thing

scores.rationale: Guinea bauxite is not a stable oligopoly for Ashapura — Chinese players hold ~90% of the business and the company is an index-linked price taker to large refinery customers.
scores.quote: only one company -- 90% of the business has been done by mostly Chinese company

scores.rationale: Concessions and self-built infrastructure are real entry barriers, but pricing has been irrational enough that restarted suspended leases and excess alumina supply drove prices down and a government quota is needed to restore balance.
scores.quote: The main reasons for the drop in the bauxite price are mainly because of some of the suspended leases in Guinea has started their operation

scores.rationale: There is no clear identification of weak competitors ceding share; the proposed quota is described as curtailing exports generally, and the India competitive set is never discussed.
scores.quote: there will be some curtail of the export of bauxite from the Guinea

scores.rationale: The company operates in unglamorous industrial minerals and in a high-risk West African jurisdiction that most non-Chinese capital avoids, and only began investor outreach in FY26.
scores.quote: we had very limited resources, and we had like unlimited ambitions, so it is a very high risk, high reward kind of a territory

scores.rationale: Products are index-priced commodities with no image-based pricing power and modest gross economics — bauxite prices fell and India margins were squeezed by sulfuric acid and fuel costs.
scores.quote: the performance of our Specialty Adsorbent Solutions business was impacted by a sharp increase in sulfuric acid prices

scores.rationale: The pitch to customers is reliability of long-term supply backed by long-term logistics and freight tie-ups and established quality, though price remains the primary commodity variable.
scores.quote: Ashapura can remain a long-term reliable supplier of bauxite

scores.rationale: Self-built ports, mining roads and a new bridge plus contracted barging and ocean freight give customers dependable delivery access, and the 100km mine-plant-port cluster in India adds to it.
scores.quote: we have made the long-term arrangements for the coming quarters or you can say the calendar year 2026, so that we will not face any such problems related with the barging, transhippers or the ocean-going vessels

scores.rationale: The customer base is entirely corporate/industrial where TCO and reliability are the right levers, and Ashapura offers reliability, but there is no evidence of switching-cost lock-in.
scores.quote: catering to several core industries... metal and foundries, oil and gas, edible oils, petrochemicals, paint and coatings

scores.rationale: The advantage claimed is resource and logistics based rather than technological; product upgrades are incremental processing steps and no R&D intensity is disclosed.
scores.quote: in India, we will go for more on the value added mineral products rather than going for the bulk exports

scores.rationale: No two-sided network exists — this is a bulk mineral extraction and export business with no self-reinforcing user dynamics mentioned in any call.

Three self-built ports with 16 mt handling capacity moving to 20 mt, 400km of roads and long-term freight contracts are hard to replicate, but larger Chinese operators in Guinea hold comparable or better reach.
scores.quote: We have built three new ports in Guinea. We have built more than 300 kilometers of high-quality heavy truck kind of roads

scores.rationale: Capital in FY26 went to deleveraging and buying out financial investors rather than growth assets, with equipment loans shrinking from INR95 crores to INR70 crores and no growth capex programme discussed.
scores.quote: Total consolidated debt as on March 31, 2026 stood at INR2,778 crores... INR70 crores of equipment loan

scores.rationale: No mention of advertising or promotional spend in any of the four calls.
No R&D spend, programme or product pipeline is discussed anywhere in the last-12-month calls.

Acquisitions were small, simple and complementary — buying out Macquarie SBI's securities in its own subsidiary ACL for INR667 crores and raising Viva Highways' stake in the Jaora-Nayagaon toll asset to 61.17% — which simplified the structure rather than adding new businesses.
scores.quote: resulting in a full acquisition of securities previously held by Macquarie SBI Infrastructure Funds. This transaction consolidates our control and simplifies the ownership structure of ACL

scores.rationale: No dividend or buyback policy is mentioned in the excerpts; monetization proceeds were applied to debt reduction instead, but distribution itself is not addressed.

Turnover fell 17% in FY26 against a flat order book (INR15,886 crores to INR15,312 crores) and management itself blamed weak fixed-overhead absorption, indicating deteriorating asset productivity with no protecting moat.
scores.quote: It's more an impact of a lower turnover and coverage of the fixed overheads which are there

scores.rationale: Revenue declined every quarter of FY26 (-30%, -11%, -18%, -10%) and the order book shrank slightly, so there is no evidence of share capture despite a fragmented market.
scores.quote: total income for the year stood at INR5,952 crores as compared to INR7,188 crores for FY '25, a degrowth of 17%

scores.rationale: Credible international wins were landed across the year — Guyana Phase 2 (USD67mn), Saudi Arabia's Diriyah hotel package (INR900 crores share), Angola T&D (USD72mn) and Liberia roads (USD45mn) — though these are competitively bid EPC contracts rather than premium brand extension.
scores.quote: receipt of letter of award in Kingdom of Saudi Arabia through our wholly owned subsidiary in a joint venture... our share of the project is INR900 crores

scores.rationale: There is no pricing-led growth: volumes and revenue fell, management cites intense competition and elevated input costs, and the only positive is a modest 130 bps standalone margin improvement from mix.
scores.quote: Execution in Q2 FY '26 was somewhat muted due to extensive monsoon and intense competition

scores.rationale: The road cycle appears near its trough — awarding subdued for two years and FY26 construction the lowest since 2017-18 — with an identifiable upturn signalled by INR75,000 crores of BOT toll projects targeted in FY27 and road capex up 8%.
scores.quote: The construction of national highways this financial year will be lowest since 2017-18... The government is also targeting approximately INR 75,000 crores of projects under the BOT toll model in FY27

scores.rationale: End markets show long-duration secular expansion — INR12-13 lakh crores railway capex to 2030, expressway network targeted to rise from ~4,500 km toward 15,000 km by FY32, and renewable-driven T&D investment — though it is government-budget dependent.
scores.quote: In railways, the government has outlined a long-term capital expenditure plan nearly INR12 lakh crores to INR13 lakh crores by 2030

scores.rationale: Management executed a coherent deleveraging: 10 HAM/BOT assets monetized in FY26 cutting consolidated debt from INR6,826 crores to INR2,778 crores, with ratings reaffirmed at AA/A1+ and no large diversifying acquisition.
scores.quote: During FY '26, the company successfully monetized 10 HAM and BOT projects, generating value and improving capital efficiency

scores.rationale: The multi-year asset-monetization and structure-simplification programme was pushed to completion despite repeated long-stop-date extensions, alongside patient diversification into railway electrification, T&D and international markets.
scores.quote: Although the earlier long stop date was June 30, both parties are working constructively towards closure under the agreed securities purchase agreement

scores.rationale: Calls are led by the MD and CFO with plain operational and order-book detail, no promotional framing or celebrity positioning, from a Nashik-headquartered promoter family.
scores.quote: Our primary focus remains on maintaining a sustainable EPC business in segments encompassing Roads, Highways, Railways, Power Transmission and Distribution as well as Buildings

scores.rationale: No discussion of talent development, succession or leadership pipeline in any of the four calls.
Management gave specific, unflattering explanations for weak execution and volunteered the INR25 crores ECL provision and the MMRDA cancellation, though it deferred on the provision's details.
scores.quote: out of 7 projects which we got only 3 have moved ahead and 4 are yet to start. So these are really reflected in the Q1 turnover degrowth

scores.rationale: Headline profit growth flatters the underlying business — 9M FY26 PAT rose 97% while operating revenue fell 20% and PBT before exceptionals was only INR150 crores — so the results reflect asset-sale gains rather than operating skill.
scores.quote: PAT stood at INR272 crores as compared to INR138 crores in 9 months FY25, up by 97%... Profit before tax before exceptional items stood at INR150 crores

scores.rationale: Work is won through competitive public tenders across roads, railways and T&D with no monopoly position in the customer's mind or aftermarket franchise.
scores.quote: Only 300 kilometers was awarded while 1,600 kilometers was under construction, but with robust pipeline and NHAI tightening contractor eligibilities

scores.rationale: The retained toll assets are genuine regional monopolies with captive traffic, and management doubled down by raising its Jaora-Nayagaon stake to 61.17%, with toll collection up 16% year-on-year in Q4.
scores.quote: increased its stake by 26% in Jaora-Nayagaon Toll Road Company Limited to 61.17%... underscoring our confidence in the asset's long-term cash flow potential

scores.rationale: This is a fragmented contracting market facing a monopsony customer (NHAI/state agencies) that sets terms and can cancel work, as shown by MMRDA scrapping the INR279 crores Kolshet project.
scores.quote: Kolshet Project of INR 279 crores cancelled by MMRDA

scores.rationale: Pricing is irrational with intense competition on a shrinking award pool, only partly offset by NHAI tightening contractor eligibility norms.
scores.quote: Execution in Q2 FY '26 was somewhat muted due to extensive monsoon and intense competition

scores.rationale: Tighter NHAI eligibility criteria are explicitly squeezing weaker-balance-sheet contractors, and Ashoka's own deleveraging to INR2,778 crores plus AA rating positions it to absorb their share.
scores.quote: NHAI tightening contractor eligibilities, larger players with strong balance sheets are well positioned

scores.rationale: The company is closely followed rather than ignored, with quarterly calls hosted by Anand Rathi, Nirmal Bang and IIFL and questions from ICICI, JM Financial and Enam.
scores.quote: welcome to the Ashoka Buildcon 3Q FY '26 Conference Call hosted by IIFL Capital

scores.rationale: There is no image- or taste-driven pricing power; standalone EBITDA margins are ~10% and fell to 9.2% in Q4 under input-cost pressure.
scores.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR168 crores, down by 7% Y-on-Y with EBITDA margins of 9.2%

scores.rationale: Repeat awards from BMC and the railways suggest clients value proven execution and prequalification, but tenders remain price-determined so trust does not displace price.
scores.quote: additional scope of work order, from the BMC toward the existing Sion-Panvel Highway flyover project, amounting to INR447 crores... reflecting continued confidence in our execution capabilities

scores.rationale: No discussion of distribution reach, accessibility or sales-force intimacy — not a meaningful dimension in tendered EPC and not addressed in the calls.

The customer base is almost entirely government agencies with no switching-cost lock-in — contracts end at completion and can be cancelled — so neither the retail-intangibles nor the corporate lock-in model applies.
scores.quote: The company has received four new project orders... from BMC and Daman Public Works Department

scores.rationale: There is some genuine technical capability — 2x25kV railway electrification for 160 kmph running and a INR1,387 crores intelligent traffic management system win via Ashoka Purestudy — but no R&D intensity or multi-product tech edge.
scores.quote: Both involve upgrading the electrification traction system to 2x25kV standard to enable high-speed rail movement up to 160 kilometers per hour

scores.rationale: Revenue is won project-by-project through tenders with no two-sided network that strengthens with scale, as the tender-by-tender order book disclosure each quarter shows.
scores.quote: the company has received four new project orders, including one additional work order

scores.rationale: Geographic reach spans India, Guyana, Saudi Arabia, Angola and Liberia, but this is project mobilization rather than a service network rivals cannot match — and mobilization itself proved a bottleneck.
scores.quote: the orders which we got in last season are still in mobilization stage

scores.rationale: FY26 capex of INR1,050 cr (~2.4% of revenue) was directed at new products, EV/battery capacity and greenfield bus plants rather than maintenance, alongside record EBITDA margin and a swing to INR5,899 cr net cash, implying high incremental returns — though absolute capex is modest and not rising sharply.
scores.quote: Capex for the quarter was at INR203 crores and cumulatively at INR1,050 crores for the year. Most of the capital expenditure has been deployed towards new products, including future technology development, alternate powertrain technologies and electric vehicles.

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend in any of the four calls.

R&D output was visible and commercial within the year — HIPPO tractors, TAURUS tippers, 280/320/360 HP powertrains, 4.1t Bada Dost, Phoenix for exports, plus CNG/LNG/hydrogen/EV variants — with management explicitly working to raise R&D throughput and cut time to market.
scores.quote: We are also working on improving the throughput of our R&D resources, which will help us reduce the time to market

scores.rationale: No operating acquisitions in the window — growth was organic (greenfield battery plant, new bus plants), with only a reverse merger of HLF into NDL Ventures for listing purposes and a JV-style MOU with PT Pindad, so there is no bolt-on track record to score either way.
scores.quote: Reverse merger of HLF with NBL Ventures is progressing as per plan and should get consummated within this or the next quarter.

scores.rationale: Two interim dividends (INR1 and INR2.50) were declared explicitly off improved fiscal performance while the balance sheet moved to INR5,899 cr net cash, a coherent if unremarkable policy; no buybacks were executed.
scores.quote: Basis standout performance of FY '26, the Board of Directors have recommended a second interim dividend of INR2.50 per share.

scores.rationale: INR44,007 cr revenue on ~INR1,050 cr annual capex with working capital cut roughly in half and net cash of INR5,899 cr indicates high asset turn for a CV OEM, protected by ~31% MHCV share and a 2,104-touchpoint service moat.
scores.quote: We have been able to keep our operating capital very lean and have brought it down by almost 50% on Y-o-Y basis.

scores.rationale: Share gains were real and repeated — MHCV up 50-60bps through 9M and LCV VAHAN up 80bps for the year to 12.7% with plenty of runway at that level — but Q4/FY26 MHCV growth was only in line with industry, so the gain decelerated at year-end.
scores.quote: full year LCV VAHAN market share stood at 12.7%, higher 80 basis points Y-o-Y

scores.rationale: Exports hit a record 18,082 units (+18.5%) with broad-based growth across GCC, Africa and SAARC, ASEAN being built as a fourth home market via PT Pindad and distributors in Malaysia/Philippines — offset by the failed UK operation being shut down.
scores.quote: Our export volumes for full year reached a historic high of 18,082 units, delivering a robust growth of 18.5%

scores.rationale: FY26 growth was overwhelmingly volume- and cycle-led (all-time high 220,437 CV units on a GST-driven industry up 12%), and mix actually hurt gross margin in Q3, with pricing/premiumization only defending margins rather than driving the topline.
scores.quote: Overall, CV volumes scaled a new all-time high of 220,437 units, surpassing the previous peak of 197,366 units achieved in FY '19.

scores.rationale: The company is at a cyclical peak, not a trough — FY26 volumes surpassed the FY19 all-time peak after a GST-triggered replacement surge — and management itself flags diesel and commodity headwinds ahead.
scores.quote: we are entering the new fiscal year with cautious optimism... mindful of the macroeconomic headwinds such as global economic uncertainties, commodity price volatility and diesel price increases

scores.rationale: Core MHCV demand is GDP-cyclical rather than secular, but genuinely structural adjacencies are compounding fast — defence revenue +84% in Q3 and +20% for the year, power solutions +16.4%, aftermarket +9.5% and EV bus leadership at Switch.
scores.quote: Revenues from defense business, including revenue from our defense subsidiary, ALDS was higher 20% Y-o-Y.

scores.rationale: Growth has been organic with no large M&A, capex held near 2% of sales, a loss-making UK operation shut rather than subsidised, subsidiary investment of just INR387 cr, and leverage reversed into INR5,899 cr net cash.
scores.quote: We had net cash of INR5,899 crores at the end of the year, an increase of more than INR1,650 crores Y-o-Y.

scores.rationale: Stated multi-year goals were actually hit — Switch India moved from EBITDA-positive to PAT-positive in FY26 exactly as guided, the mid-teen EBITDA ambition reached 13%, and long-cycle bets (battery plant, EV plant built in 14 months, ASEAN home market) were funded through the cycle.
scores.quote: Our EV subsidiary, Switch Mobility India delivered a standout performance, attaining net profitability in FY '26

scores.rationale: Commentary is largely operational and metric-driven, but management volunteered its own share-price high in the opening remarks and repeatedly cited ESG rankings, which is not the substance-over-visibility posture the parameter rewards.
scores.quote: Incidentally, in this quarter, our share price also touched its ever-highest mark in the third week of September.

scores.rationale: The calls discuss CSR education programmes but say nothing about internal talent development or leadership pipeline.

Management proactively disclosed unflattering items — the INR308 cr labour-code charge, 70-100bps gross-margin compression with named causes, the UK redundancy programme, HLF merger delays and March export logistics problems — while consistently separating exceptional items.
scores.quote: Reverse merger of HLF with NDL Ventures had some initial delays

scores.rationale: The record results coincided with an exceptional exogenous tailwind — GST 2.0 rate cuts driving industry MHCV volumes up 21-24% — and in the strongest quarters Ashok Leyland merely grew in line with that industry, so results overstate incremental management skill.
scores.quote: The GST reset provided the much-needed trigger for fresh CV replacement cycle to kick in.

scores.rationale: Clear leadership in MHCV buses at 34.1% share and a steadily growing aftermarket (+9.5% for the year) give a strong niche position, but nothing approaching a monopoly in the customer's mind across the core truck business.
scores.quote: MHCV bus volume was 20,840 units with a market share of 34.1%. Ashok Leyland continued its leadership position in MHCV buses.

scores.rationale: Some captive-aftermarket and regional density effects exist via the service network and in-house financing, but truck buyers face low switching costs and the calls show share moving between OEMs each quarter.
scores.quote: Domestic aftermarket revenue for the quarter was up 11.2% Y-o-Y and higher 9.5% for the full year.

scores.rationale: The Indian MHCV market is a stable few-player oligopoly in which Ashok Leyland holds ~30-31% share year after year and can push through price increases, though large fleet buyers retain real bargaining power.
scores.quote: Ashok Leyland domestic MHCV volume grew in line with industry with market share of a healthy 30.8% for the year.

scores.rationale: No new entrants are mentioned in four calls, and pricing behaviour is rational — the industry passed on AC-mandate and commodity costs, with Ashok Leyland citing better price realisation rather than discounting as its margin lever.
scores.quote: This was made possible through better price realizations, rigorous cost-saving efforts and continued focus on improving product and business mix.

scores.rationale: Share was demonstrably taken from weaker competitors in both segments — LCV volumes +30% in Q3 and +23% in Q4 against slower industry growth — and at 12.7% LCV share there is a large pool of weaker players left to take from.
scores.quote: Ashok Leyland domestic LCV volume for quarter 3 was at 20,518 units, higher by 30% year-on-year, beating industry growth.

scores.rationale: This is a heavily covered large-cap — calls hosted by Axis, BNP Paribas, ICICI and Avendus, an all-time-high share price and top-2% global DJSI ranking — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: our share price also touched its ever-highest mark

scores.rationale: Trucks are bought on economics, not image — material cost runs at 71.4% of revenue (gross margin ~28.6%) and every product claim is framed in payload, TCO and turnaround time rather than brand desirability.
scores.quote: Material cost as a percentage of revenue for Q4 was 71.4%

scores.rationale: The premiumization pitch is explicitly reliability and uptime — 'unmatched reliability', industry-best TAT/TCO, and a service transformation that lifted the company to No.1 on dealer satisfaction — though price still matters materially to fleet buyers.
scores.quote: These new trucks are built with next-level of heavy-duty aggregates, delivering unmatched reliability.

scores.rationale: Distribution intimacy is a deliberate, funded programme: over 200 touchpoints added in FY26 to reach 2,104, deliberately weighted 45% to under-penetrated North/Northeast markets, backed by in-house financing that closes sales at the point of contact.
scores.quote: At the end of FY '26, Ashok Leyland network has a total of 2,104 touch points, 1,159 for MHCV and 945 for LCV.

scores.rationale: The customer base is corporate/fleet and the benefit set is correctly matched to it — TCO, uptime and earnings-per-month arguments plus HLF captive financing that locks in the relationship.
scores.quote: HLF's strong performance not only contributed to our consolidated results, but also enabled vehicle sales through continued financing support to our customers.

scores.rationale: A genuinely broad multi-powertrain portfolio (diesel 280-360HP, electric trucks and buses, CNG, LNG, hydrogen) plus in-house innovations like IVAC and a new battery-pack plant, but R&D intensity is modest and the edge is breadth rather than depth versus global peers.
scores.quote: We are also ready with products on other greener technologies, such as CNG, LNG and even hydrogen.

scores.rationale: Nothing in the business model is two-sided or self-reinforcing with scale — value comes from manufacturing scale and service reach, not from users attracting other users.

A 2,104-touchpoint domestic service network expanding into North/Northeast, four international home markets with local presence, and captive financing constitute reach that new or smaller rivals cannot replicate in a business where service uptime decides repeat purchase.
scores.quote: Our approach of developing strong local presence and building products suiting the local requirements.

scores.rationale: Large committed growth/backward-integration capex is underway (VAM-VAE emulsion at Dahej, white cement plant in Dubai, described as ongoing into next year), but returns are pitched as cost efficiency rather than demonstrated incremental ROIC.
scores.quote: These are big projects where significant CapEx has been committed.

scores.rationale: A&P was deliberately stepped up all year and aimed at durable equity — BCCI colour partnership, Har Ghar, KBC, Big Boss, Spotify, digital shift — and management explicitly links it to consumer mind-share.
scores.quote: a very big upsurge with respect to the overall spending on the brand, building the brand equity and really spending for getting the share of the consumer's mind

scores.rationale: R&D visibly converts into commercialised products — new products are 14-15% of revenue, 160+ patents, and world-first launches like PU Gold anti-termite, Nilaya Arc and graphene exteriors.
scores.quote: Today, we speak of more than 160 patents of what we have put into the market.

scores.rationale: No acquisition of any kind is mentioned across the four calls in the window.
Dividends, buybacks or distribution policy are not discussed in any of the excerpts.

The brand/distribution moat is strong, but the current strategy is deliberately adding heavy fixed assets via backward integration (Dahej emulsion, Dubai white cement), which works against asset-lightness.
scores.quote: the whole space of backward integration has also been very significant for us and a huge amount of investments are taking place in this area

scores.rationale: Asian Paints is already the dominant incumbent so runway to gain share is limited, and this year's decorative print — 3.9% volume with -1.2% value — shows defence rather than capture.
scores.quote: We've got about 3.9% volume growth over the Q1 of last year… the value is just about -1.2%.

scores.rationale: Expansion talk is intra-India regionalisation rather than new geographies; the only overseas item is a Dubai white cement plant, which is an input asset, not market entry.
scores.quote: we have put up a white cement plant which is coming up in Dubai

scores.rationale: Growth is volume-led with negative price/mix — value growth trailed volume into negative territory and management conceded down-trading out of luxury emulsions.
scores.quote: when we look at luxury emulsions… there was a little bit of down-trading which was happening in the market

scores.rationale: The company appears to be past the trough — several depressed quarters, then a sequential uptick, urban green shoots and an accelerating B2B/infra engine.
scores.quote: some of the overall demand being depressed over the last three or four quarters, we saw a slight uptick in demand sequentially

scores.rationale: B2B is tied to structural government infrastructure and private capex cycles (airports, ports, tunnels), though the core decorative market showed cyclical softness rather than secular expansion.
scores.quote: every airport, every port, every tunnel which we are approaching and looking at participating in the growth story where government is putting a lot of money

scores.rationale: Strategy is entirely organic — brand, innovation, services, regionalisation and self-built backward integration with no M&A — and investment was pushed through a weak demand year, though leverage is never addressed.
scores.quote: a series of initiatives which we had basically put into place for accelerating growth and not looking at what the external conditions would be

scores.rationale: Multi-year commitments are sustained independently of the cycle — 23 years of ColourNext research, 10 years of St+art murals, and a multi-year backward-integration programme — but this window's delivery was flat on value.
scores.quote: The other big area that we have been working on for the last 23 years… This is our ColourNext property

scores.rationale: No personality cult around the CEO, but the calls lean heavily on celebrity-led properties and self-congratulatory framing rather than understated substance.
scores.quote: So, I think this was really a master move

scores.rationale: Talent development, succession or the internal leadership pipeline are not mentioned anywhere in the four calls.
Q1 openly flagged the value shortfall, monsoon impact and a luxury miss, though later quarters shift toward initiative narrative with less numeric self-criticism.
scores.quote: When we look at luxury emulsions, I think here we did not do as per our expectations.

scores.rationale: The narrative of disruption and unparalleled differentiation runs well ahead of the delivered numbers (negative decorative value growth, down-trading), so results should not be read as proof of skill.
scores.quote: So, these are the six big areas, very different, very disruptive

scores.rationale: Genuine mind-monopoly evidence: a proprietary product has become the category generic, alongside the self-described largest painting service in the world.
scores.quote: now Damp Proof has become generic to the category

scores.rationale: Retail decorative paint carries little switching cost, though B2B annuity services (Total Assure, Metacare factory maintenance) create some captive aftermarket lock-in.
scores.quote: we today maintain factories for most of the bigger players in various industries

scores.rationale: The calls reference competition and consumer down-trading but never characterise industry structure or pricing power over the end customer, so an oligopoly premium is not evidenced.
scores.quote: quality, which is far better in terms of what possibly the competition offers

scores.rationale: Execution-based barriers exist (regional pack logistics claimed hard to replicate), but negative value growth alongside positive volume and affordable-price-point pushes point to a competitive pricing environment.
scores.quote: regional packs, which is a huge logistical exercise, very difficult to replicate by any other player

scores.rationale: No weak or retreating competitor is identified in any of the four calls.
The opposite of under-the-radar — national cricket sponsorship, mass-media properties and celebrity campaigns make it one of India's most visible consumer franchises.
scores.quote: we became the colour partner to the team India

scores.rationale: Strong emotional/aspirational positioning and a super-luxury ladder (Nilaya Arc, signature collections) exist, but demonstrated pricing power weakened as customers down-traded and value growth turned negative.
scores.quote: we invoked Har Ghar very strongly because we know that that's the emotional connect

scores.rationale: The proposition is explicitly built on certainty — 10-year warranties, supervision-led Total Assure and Smart Assure, and Metacare asset protection where trust, not price, is the purchase driver.
scores.quote: we look at standing by the customer… something which gives the customer a strong confidence

scores.rationale: Access and intimacy are exceptional — roughly 1.7 lakh retail outlets plus a direct painting service reaching 650+ towns.
scores.quote: this is now closer to about 1.7 lakh retail outlets

scores.rationale: Benefits are correctly matched by customer type: emotional/aspirational branding for retail, and technical solutions, warranty and supervised service platforms for corporate and government buyers.
scores.quote: we are able to offer solutions which are technical in nature, at the same time with a certain expertise and warranty

scores.rationale: A real multi-product technology edge is claimed and evidenced (Lotus effect, graphene exteriors, world-first PU Gold, VAM-VAE emulsion), but the claims are self-reported and have not yet shown up in premium realisation.
scores.quote: We have launched for the first time in the world an anti-termite finish called "PU Gold"

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network dynamic is described in the excerpts.
Reach rivals cannot easily match — ~1.7 lakh outlets, a 650+ town service footprint, and region-specific pack logistics management calls very difficult to replicate.
scores.quote: We really inflated our beautiful home service in terms of its reach. Looking at more than 650+ towns

scores.rationale: FY26 capex of ~Rs. 500 Cr (Karoli expansion, new Bangalore plant, brake pad capacity to 32 Cr units, captive solar) is clearly growth-oriented and is converting into returns — ROACE 26.9% and ROE 25.3% in FY26 with the new Bangalore plant EBITDA-positive within two quarters of commissioning.
scores.quote: We had planned Rs. 450 crore initially in the FY26... but still we will close the CAPEX at Rs. 500 crore

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend in any of the four calls.
R&D spend, pipeline or new-product development economics are never quantified or discussed in the last-12-months calls.
No acquisition was announced, contemplated or discussed in the window, so there is no M&A execution to judge.

A modest, consistent dividend of Rs. 1.85 per Rs. 2 share against FY26 EPS of Rs. 15.08 (~12% payout) with no buyback — coherent retention given 26.9% ROACE, but no evidence of opportunistic or disciplined capital-return policy.
scores.quote: The board has recommended a dividend of 92.5%, that is Rs. 1.85 per equity share of face value of Rs. 2 each

scores.rationale: This is a capital-intensive casting/component business — Rs. 500 Cr capex on ~Rs. 4,200 Cr revenue and multi-quarter plant ramp-ups — so it is not asset-light, though returns are high at 26.9% ROACE.
scores.quote: We have delivered strong returns in FY26 with ROACE at 26.9% and ROE at 25.3%

scores.rationale: Net revenue grew 20.1% in FY26 versus 11.8% two-wheeler industry production growth, with all three segments outgrowing the industry and brake pad share still only 10-12%, so there is both demonstrated capture and remaining runway.
scores.quote: We have outperformed the two-wheeler industry production growth of FY26... our market share should be around between 10%-12%

scores.rationale: Exports were guided to grow 20% in FY26 but instead declined from Rs. 147 Cr to Rs. 141 Cr, with the shortfall admitted; geographic expansion is the one area where guidance was repeatedly missed.
scores.quote: We could not achieve our target on the export front

scores.rationale: Growth is volume-led plus aluminium pass-through (8% of Q4 revenue growth was pure alloy price pass-through with no absolute EBITDA benefit), offset by a genuine mix improvement out of low-margin wheel assembly into value-added aluminium light-weighting.
scores.quote: Excluding pass-through impact of significant increase in aluminium prices on revenue, which was 8%

scores.rationale: The two-wheeler cycle is at or past its all-time peak, not near a bottom — FY26 production of 26.7 million units surpassed the previous FY19 peak — so the cyclical tailwind is largely spent.
scores.quote: this year the two-wheeler industry production volumes have surpassed the previous peak of FY19

scores.rationale: The end market has genuine structural supports — GST 2.0 cutting the rate on all its products from 28% to 18%, income tax rationalisation, rate cuts and rising rural income — with management framing GST 2.0 as a long-duration structural shift.
scores.quote: GST 2.0 being a structural reform, the benefit of which will accrue over a long period of time

scores.rationale: Purely organic growth with no acquisitions, deliberate multi-year exit from the low-margin wheel assembly business completed exactly as promised, and capex trimmed for FY27 — all funded alongside 25.3% ROE.
scores.quote: Strategic reduction in low margin wheel assembly business is now complete. From 1st April 2026, wheel assembly revenue will be nil

scores.rationale: Multi-year commitments were seen through — the Bangalore plant ramped from commissioning to EBITDA-positive and cash-positive within two quarters, Karoli utilisation rose steadily, the wheel-assembly exit ran to completion, and captive solar was added — under the same promoter leadership across the five-year history.
scores.quote: This facility is ramping up fast and expected to achieve 60% capacity utilization by Q2 FY26 and this facility will be cash positive in Q2 FY26 itself

scores.rationale: Calls are workmanlike and operationally detailed — plant utilisation, alloy pass-through, capex line items — with no promotional or celebrity framing beyond routine congratulation from analysts.
scores.quote: Our EBITDA margin is affected by aluminum alloy prices... however, our absolute EBITDA number remains the same

scores.rationale: The leadership pipeline is family-concentrated rather than systematically developed — three of the four Managing Directors appointed in FY2026 are Rathees, while the externally hired CEO Shalender Singh Birla exited after a single year, and no talent-development programme is discussed on any call.
scores.quote: MR. KULDIP SINGH RATHEE – CHAIRMAN AND MANAGING DIRECTOR, MR. PRASHANT RATHEE – JOINT MANAGING DIRECTOR, MR. AMAN RATHEE – JOINT MANAGING DIRECTOR

scores.rationale: Management quantifies unflattering effects rather than hiding them (alloy denominator drag on margin, 30bps and 80bps), openly owns the missed export target, and corrects an analyst's misunderstanding by pointing back to prior guidance — though the habit of restating growth ex-wheel-assembly and ex-aluminium consistently flatters the headline.
scores.quote: We could not achieve our target on the export front

scores.rationale: The record is strong but not cleanly separable from a cyclical upswing — industry production grew 11.8% to an all-time peak in the same year, and much of the margin gain came from mechanically shedding a loss-making business rather than from operating skill alone.
scores.quote: strategic reduction in low-value added wheel assembly business

scores.rationale: Sustained leadership in advanced braking systems and a genuine branded position against duplicators in the aftermarket, but the position is not monopoly-like everywhere — brake pad share is only 10-12%.
scores.quote: We have sustained our market leadership position in the advanced braking system

scores.rationale: OEM qualification for safety-critical braking parts implies some switching cost and the independent aftermarket grew 24.7%, but there is no evidence of a captive lock-in strong enough to price independently — management must still ask OEMs to absorb input costs.
scores.quote: The customers have been requested to support, and we are confident that all our prestigious OEMs will compensate this

scores.rationale: The end customers are large two-wheeler OEMs who clearly hold the negotiating power — cost increases must be 'requested' and aluminium moves purely as pass-through with no absolute margin gain to ASK.
scores.quote: We are getting the aluminum prices, whatever is the raw material cost plus the value addition

scores.rationale: Pricing is rational and formula-based (raw material cost plus value addition, accepted by OEMs) and GST 2.0 is formalising the market against unorganised entrants, though the persistence of grey-market duplicators shows entry into the aftermarket is not hard.
scores.quote: the reduction of GST rate from 28% to 18% is helping us to outgrow in the Indian aftermarket and capture more market share from grey market operators and duplicators

scores.rationale: Management names an explicit, sizeable pool of weak competitors it is taking share from, and quantifies the result — independent aftermarket revenue up 24.7% in FY26.
scores.quote: our independent aftermarket has grown by 24.7% in FY26

scores.rationale: Not obscure — the company has been listed since 2023 and its calls draw questions from CLSA and Nuvama, though it remains a fairly plain mid-cap ancillary rather than a crowded story.
scores.quote: The first question is from the line of Rishi Kapadia from CLSA India Private Limited

scores.rationale: There is some brand pull against duplicators in the aftermarket, but no image-driven pricing power at the OEM level — margins sit at ~13% EBITDA and input costs move straight through to the customer.
scores.quote: Upward increase in prices of aluminum affects our EBITDA percentage because of the denominator effect

scores.rationale: The products are safety-critical (braking, safety control cables) supplied under IATF/ISO certification to 'prestigious OEMs', and the aftermarket share gain is explicitly against duplicators — customers are buying certified reliability over cheap copies.
scores.quote: gain more market share from grey market operators and duplicators

scores.rationale: Capacity is deliberately placed next to customer clusters (Manesar, Karoli in Rajasthan, new Bangalore plant) and the independent aftermarket channel grew 24.7%, indicating strengthening reach and customer proximity.
scores.quote: benefit from increasing capacity utilization at Karoli and New Bangalore facility

scores.rationale: The mix is well matched — corporate OEM customers served on reliability and cost pass-through, alongside a fast-growing retail aftermarket where the genuine-part proposition wins share from duplicators.
scores.quote: our independent aftermarket has grown by 24.7% in FY26

scores.rationale: The edge described is manufacturing and process based — advanced braking systems and aluminium light-weighting precision solutions — with no R&D intensity, patents or product pipeline discussed to support a technology moat.
scores.quote: The Aluminium light-weighting precision solutions revenue grew by 47% in Q4 FY26 and 30% in FY26

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network dynamic is present or discussed in this business model.

The independent aftermarket network is delivering 24.7% growth and taking share from the unorganised trade, backed by plants co-located with OEM hubs — a real reach advantage, though not demonstrated to be unmatchable by rivals.
scores.quote: the reduction of GST rate from 28% to 18% is especially good for ASK because it will help us to outgrow in the Indian aftermarket

scores.rationale: Large, clearly growth-oriented bed expansion (373-560 beds added in the year, 4,445-bed pipeline to 15,000+ beds) is being funded while returns rise — mature hospitals at 35% ROCE and combined ROCE up 293bps to 21.1%.
