scores.rationale: Consistent long-horizon framing across all four calls — insisting the business be judged annually not quarterly, and building injectables as a multi-year platform through a loss-making ramp rather than cutting it.
scores.quote: our business is best evaluated on a long-term or at least on an annualized basis rather than quarter-on-quarter

scores.rationale: Promoter-family management communicates in plain operational terms with no self-promotion, celebrity positioning, or grandstanding across all four calls, even hosting calls through mid-tier brokers.
scores.quote: FY26 was a challenging year for Concord, and we have faced some industry headwinds

scores.rationale: No evidence of a systematic internal talent pipeline — the CFO seat turned over with an external hire (Lalit Sethi out, Raviraj Karia in), and the only talent-development reference is an industry-level government programme.
scores.quote: we are pleased to welcome Mr. Raviraj Karia as our Chief Financial Officer

scores.rationale: Management itemised each revenue miss by cause quarter after quarter and volunteered inconvenient nuance rather than spinning it, though repeated ex-start-up-cost margin framing and an H2 recovery promise that Q4 (-24%) did not deliver temper the score.
scores.quote: this was not a case of pent-up demand where all deferred supplies could be immediately executed upon resumption

scores.rationale: Skill signals (clean USFDA/EU/Russian/NAFDAC/WHO-GMP inspections, new approvals) are separable from results, but the persistent 'adjusted 40% EBITDA' framing alongside reported 35% and 12% degrowth is exactly the halo risk to discount.
scores.quote: if we exclude the impact of expenses related to our new formulation facility and expenses pertaining to our U.S. subsidiary, Stellon, our EBITDA would have been in the range of around 40.4%

scores.rationale: Near-unique global position in fermentation APIs — one of very few companies making 30+ fermentation APIs, with newly commercialised products like Fusidic Acid facing limited competition.
scores.quote: Concord remains one of the few companies globally producing more than 30 fermentation APIs

scores.rationale: High regulatory switching costs are visible in both directions — customers must qualify a DMF-linked source, which is why second-source wins are slow but sticky once secured, and why the company expects to keep the Middle East tender when it reopens.
scores.quote: we will be the preferred supplier to them

scores.rationale: Niches have few players, but customers are large generic firms and government tender bodies with real negotiating power — they unilaterally staggered procurement and put tenders in abeyance during the year.
scores.quote: customers adopted a differentiated procurement strategy, shifting from bulk purchases to a more staggered quarter-on-quarter procurement approach

scores.rationale: Entry barriers are high — fermentation capability plus a stack of USFDA, EU-GMP, Russian GMP, NAFDAC and WHO-GMP clearances — and pricing behaviour appears rational with management explicitly denying any pricing pressure in a down year.
scores.quote: successfully completed U.S. FDA, EU GMP, Russian GMP, NAFDAC and WHO-GMP inspections across multiple facilities

scores.rationale: Weaker/higher-cost incumbents exist to take from — limited European competition in Fusidic Acid and customers actively relocating supply away from existing chains post-tariff clarity.
scores.quote: We have also commercialized manufacturing of Fusidic Acid, which is having limited competition, especially from the European region.

scores.rationale: The business sits in an unglamorous, technically hard fermentation-API niche with deliberately complex, low-competition products rather than crowded high-visibility segments.
scores.quote: We continue to focus on manufacturing niche and complex products with limited competition.

scores.rationale: Margins are high (~40% ex start-up costs) but this is B2B ingredient supply where the premium comes from qualification and compliance, not image or taste, and demand proved interruptible during the year.
scores.quote: our EBITDA margin stands at a solid 41%

scores.rationale: The core customer proposition is certainty of compliant, uninterrupted supply — repeatedly evidenced by regulatory clearances framed as supply-continuity credentials and chronic therapies where customers cannot tolerate disruption.
scores.quote: These approvals position us to ensure uninterrupted supply to global markets without regulatory hurdles.

scores.rationale: Direct-access capability is only just being built — Stellon (US) and Concord Lifegen (India) were incorporated within this window and have yet to demonstrate any distribution or customer-intimacy advantage.
scores.quote: Stellon will manage end-to-end commercial operations

scores.rationale: Customers are corporate (generic majors, innovators, government tenders) and the benefit offered matches correctly — regulatory reliability and DMF-based qualification lock-in rather than consumer intangibles.
scores.quote: we have commenced supplies of our APIs to 2 innovator companies

scores.rationale: Deep, multi-product fermentation technology edge — 30+ fermentation APIs across therapeutic areas and 138+ DMFs — though R&D intensity is not quantified in these calls.
scores.quote: We have now filed over 138 DMFs and secured approvals for our ANDAs across key international markets

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network dynamic is discussed anywhere in the four calls.
Distribution has historically been via partners and the own-channel build (Stellon, Lifegen) is brand-new and unproven; regulatory reach, not distribution reach, is the actual advantage today.
scores.quote: incorporated and acquired licenses for Stellon Biotech, our U.S. subsidiary

scores.rationale: Multiple large growth projects delivered on schedule in the window — Kakinada 2,000 tpd sulphuric and 650 tpd phos acid commissioned in March 2026 with captive power, a 1 mn-ton granulation train on track for Q4, plus Senegal mining, Technical MAP and seaweed granulation — all backward-integration/capacity adds rather than maintenance.
scores.quote: In March month, company successfully commissioned the 2,000 tons per day Sulphuric acid plant and 650 tons per day Phosphoric acid plant at Kakinada, strengthening its backward integration capabilities.

scores.rationale: Promotion is field-level rather than media spend — farmer-connect, channel engagement and seed marketing in new northern markets — and it is demonstrably converting into volume growth of 24-30% in those geographies.
scores.quote: We continue to expand our footprint across North and Central India markets by active channel engagement and farmer-connect initiatives and registered a growth of more than 24% in these markets.

scores.rationale: No R&D spend disclosure, but a steady stream of differentiated products (GroPlus, GroAlpha, Urea-SSP, nano, biologicals, unique NPK grades at 35-36% of volume) shows R&D translating into saleable premium products.
scores.quote: differentiated grades like GroPlus and GroAlpha, contributing to more than 50% of the volume

scores.rationale: Only inorganic activity in the window is raising its stake in the Senegal rock phosphate mining entity to 71.5% — a small, simple, vertically complementary bolt-on that is stabilised and scaling, with no large or diversifying deals.
scores.quote: The company also has enhanced its stake in Senegalese entity and currently holding 71.5% in the mining company.

scores.rationale: The four calls contain no discussion of dividends, buybacks or any distribution policy.

This is a heavily asset-intensive business — large acid/granulation plants, captive power and an overseas mine — and Q1FY27 showed the fixed-asset burden clearly when utilisation was cut to 72% on input costs, so high asset turn is not the model.
scores.quote: We have taken a conscious call to moderate production to 6.9 lakh tons compared to 8.4 lakh tons, roughly representing 72% of capacity utilization

scores.rationale: Share gains are explicit and repeated across the window: FY26 consumption share of 17.5% making it the largest phosphatic player, and Q1FY27 primary share up to 22% from 18% with point-of-sale share to 16%, from a base well short of dominance.
scores.quote: increasing the primary market share to 22% compared to 18% in the last year

scores.rationale: Deliberate, executed expansion out of the southern base into North and Central India (4 lakh tons YTD, +30%, then +24% for FY26) built on multi-year seed marketing, plus upstream Senegal and an SSP facility being evaluated there for international markets.
scores.quote: sales have grown to 4 lakh tons, a 30% growth over last year especially from the northern markets. These were not catered to in the past - we have done seed marketing and the results are paying off.

scores.rationale: Mix is genuinely improving (unique grades 33%→36%, differentiated SSP >50%), but realisations are subsidy/MRP-bound and the only price action taken was cost pass-through that still did not cover input inflation.
scores.quote: we took some price correction during this quarter by 3% to 4% to offset the impact of increase in input prices and currency depreciation

scores.rationale: The sector is visibly near a trough — Middle East supply disruption, sulphur/ammonia spikes, phos acid at $1,700 vs $1,360, deficit monsoon and industry production down 21% — with identifiable upside from an expected NBS revision and normalising supply, though the timing rests on government action.
scores.quote: The government has made note of this issue, and we hope we get the updated NBS rates for the kharif season, which should help to improve the viability for NP, NPK fertilizers.

scores.rationale: Total phosphatic consumption is flat at ~24 mn tons, so the end market is not expanding; the structural tailwind is the mix shift toward NPK (50%→60-64%) which favours Coromandel's NP/NPK-led capacity.
scores.quote: the share of NPK moved up to 60% from what it used to be 50% 2 years before

scores.rationale: Organic, backward-integration-led capital allocation with no large M&A, and demonstrably counter-cyclical operating discipline — cutting production and sulphur usage rather than chasing volume into a loss-making input spike, and moderating sales in AP/Telangana to match consumption.
scores.quote: the company took a conscious call to moderate phos acid production and ensure that the prices of sulphur reach a reasonable level to be competitive on sourcing

scores.rationale: Long-gestation bets were carried to completion in this window — Senegal mine stabilised and now the largest exporter from that country, Kakinada integration commissioned on the promised timeline, and granulation tracking to the date given three quarters earlier.
scores.quote: Happy to note that granulation project is progressing well - as planned, we are on track for commissioning this in Q4 of this year.

scores.rationale: Commentary across all four calls is operational and metric-led — production tonnes, acid prices, reservoir levels — with credit given to government coordination and industry rather than to management, and no promotional or personality-driven framing.
scores.quote: An empowered committee comprising of government and industry officials have been working in close coordination for fertilizer production, planning and raw material sourcing.

scores.rationale: Beyond safety awards there is no discussion of talent development, and the five-year record shows a revolving door at the top — four different Managing Directors and two CFOs since FY2021 — which argues against a settled internal leadership pipeline.
scores.quote: one of our largest fertilizer plant has been given British Safety Council Five-Star Rating

scores.rationale: Management volunteers bad news plainly — calling it a tough quarter, disclosing a share slip to 14% and the resulting channel inventory build, and stating outright that current input prices are unviable rather than talking around them.
scores.quote: Our consumption-based market share in Q3 moderated to 14% as against last year 15%, which has slightly taken up our channel inventory.

scores.rationale: Results are heavily conditioned by monsoon, NBS rates and raw material cycles that management does not control, so skill is hard to isolate — though share gains and on-time project delivery amid an industry production decline are attributable to execution rather than the environment.
scores.quote: This sort of subdued subsidy rates, especially for NP/NPK fertilizers have impacted production and imports during the quarter, which were down by 21% and 38%, respectively.

scores.rationale: Some brand-led positions exist (SSP leadership, GroPlus/Urea-SSP, unique grades at ~35%), but the core NPK/DAP product is a subsidised commodity sold against 10 mn tons of imports, so nothing approaching a monopoly in the farmer's mind.
scores.quote: Industry also resorted to a higher level of imports, both DAP and NPK, which added up to 10 million tons against previous year of 7 million tons.

scores.rationale: Coromandel holds a regionally concentrated stronghold in the southern markets with a dense retail and channel presence that lets it shift volume between states, though farmer-level switching costs are low.
scores.quote: The company has performed very well in Maharashtra, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, offsetting some drop in Andhra.

scores.rationale: The largest player holds only ~17.5% consumption share and pricing is set by government NBS rates and MRP rather than by industry structure, so this is neither a concentrated nor a price-setting oligopoly.
scores.quote: making us the largest player with the highest market share of 17.5% in the phosphatic sector in the country

scores.rationale: Entry barriers are real — capital-intensive acid/granulation assets, scarce rock and ammonia access, and subsidy registration — and pricing behaviour is rational (industry passed on GST cuts, took a measured 3-4% correction), but import competition and government-set economics cap the benefit.
scores.quote: industry has passed on the benefits of these rate revisions to the farming community

scores.rationale: Weaker competitors are visibly retreating — industry production and imports fell 21% and 38% in Q1FY27 on unviable subsidy economics — while Coromandel, integrated and raw-material-covered, raised primary share from 18% to 22%.
scores.quote: Commissioning of these plants has happened at a very opportune time, and this has ensured that we continue to produce and make phosphate fertilisers available to farmers when industry is facing shortage of key raw materials.

scores.rationale: This is the largest phosphatic player in India, covered every quarter by major brokerages (PhillipCapital, IIFL, Elara, Antique) and operating inside a heavily policy-scrutinised sector — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: welcome to Coromandel International Limited Q1 FY27 Earnings Conference Call

scores.rationale: Some premiumisation exists via differentiated grades, but MRP is administratively capped and margins were compressed by ammonia/sulphur spikes the subsidy did not cover, so there is no image-driven pricing power.
scores.quote: Fertilizer business margins were under pressure due to sudden spurt in key input raw materials like ammonia and sulphur.

scores.rationale: Assured supply is a genuine differentiator in this sector and Coromandel delivered it — record production and availability while peers cut output during the raw material shortage — though the farmer remains highly price/MRP sensitive.
scores.quote: The company achieved highest ever quarterly fertilizer production of 9.9 lakh tons, which is 18% up over the last year.

scores.rationale: Direct farmer intimacy is a stated strength — own retail centres, Gromor drone spraying across ~3 lakh acres, and channel/farmer engagement that opened entirely new northern geographies.
scores.quote: Coromandel's drone spraying service delivered through Gromor drive initiative and also through our own retail centers, covered close to 3 lakh acres and is witnessing strong adoption by the farming community.

scores.rationale: The customer is the retail farmer and the benefit set is matched appropriately — branded differentiated grades plus service (drones, retail centres, agronomy engagement) — but the economics are ultimately mediated by the government subsidy payer, diluting the lock-in.
scores.quote: Our share of unique grades has improved from 33% to 36% during the quarter.

scores.rationale: There is meaningful process technology in the new phos acid plant aimed at optimising low-grade rock use, plus nano and biological product lines, but this is process/product incrementalism rather than a deep multi-product technology edge.
scores.quote: Phosphoric acid operations are getting stabilized, and we are embarking on the new technology implemented to ensure optimum utilization of rock.

scores.rationale: Nothing in the business model is self-reinforcing with scale — fertilizer is a physical, per-transaction sale, and the emerging data layer (QR traceability, Agri-Stack) is government-owned rather than Coromandel's network.
scores.quote: The government has also initiated a pilot implementation of National Fertilizer sales framework, introducing QR code-enabled traceability across fertilizer transactions

scores.rationale: Reach is the clearest moat — a southern retail and dealer network extended into North/Central India, own retail centres and drone services, letting it convert supply availability into share gains competitors could not match.
scores.quote: The point of sales increased by 13% to 7.9 lakh tons, resulting in market share improving to 16%.

scores.rationale: Clear growth (not maintenance) capex — 400mn tablet/capsule capacity commissioned Dec 2025, a new 600-kg line and a dedicated hormone plant due Q1/Q2 FY27 — funded internally while ROCE ran 41% (FY26) and the company stayed net cash.
scores.quote: capacity of around 400 million tablets and capsules which was recently commissioned at our Gujarat facility in December 2025

scores.rationale: No explicit A&P disclosure, but brand-building spend via field force and prescriber engagement is visibly rising and converting into brand equity (two brands crossed INR 100cr, eight in the 50-100cr club).
scores.quote: increase in the corresponding other expenses related to medical reps

scores.rationale: R&D spend stepped up in Q4FY26 and demonstrably yields output — new-product launches contributed 6.4% of FY26 growth vs 2.5% for IPM, plus first entry into biosimilars with three launches.
scores.quote: growth from new product launches for CORONA stood at 6.4%, which is almost 2.6x more compared to overall 2.5% growth for IPM

scores.rationale: Small complementary brand bolt-ons (seven Bayer-Zydus trademarks, Wokadine ranked #2 in povidone iodine) added to a track record of scaling brands bought from GSK/Abbott/Sanofi, with FY26 EBITDA margin still up 80bps.
scores.quote: The acquisition of Wokadine, which is ranked 2 in the Indian Povidone Iodine market, enables us to enter into the 630 plus crore Povidone Iodine market

scores.rationale: A maiden 100% dividend (INR 10/share) in the first year post-listing signals intent to distribute, but there is no buyback record or articulated long-run policy to judge discipline against.
scores.quote: We are delighted to announce 100% dividend, which is equal to ₹10 per share for FY26

scores.rationale: Branded-formulation model turns INR 1,403cr revenue on a modest two-plant asset base with ROCE ~41% and ROE 29%, protected by prescription stickiness in chronic therapies, though capacity build-out is currently absorbing capital.
scores.quote: our return ratios also remained robust, with RoCE at almost 41% in FY26 and RoE at 29.2%

scores.rationale: Small base with long runway (addresses only ~one-third of IPM, ranked 27th) yet is the fastest grower among the top 30, moving 30th→28th→27th while growing at ~2x IPM.
scores.quote: CORONA continues to be the fastest-growing pharmaceutical company among the top 30 companies in IPM. Our industry ranking has improved to 27th position

scores.rationale: EAEU GMP certification opens five Eurasian markets via B2B, but management concedes dossiers take 1-2 years and international will stay ~10% of mix, so it is optionality rather than executed expansion.
scores.quote: For dossier to get the approval will take another 1-2 years and then the business starts

scores.rationale: Growth is explicitly volume- and new-introduction-led rather than price/mix-led — FY26 volumes +3% and NI +6.4%, with management stressing volume as the differentiator and denying any extraordinary pricing action.
scores.quote: An important and differentiating factor driving our overall growth is volume

scores.rationale: IPM is coming off a soft patch (8.6% FY26, 0.7% volume growth) into five consecutive months of double-digit growth, an identifiable industry upturn CORONA is levered to, though pharma is only mildly cyclical.
scores.quote: IPM, the industry has recorded double-digit growth over the past five months, which is an extremely positive development

scores.rationale: 72% of revenue sits in structurally expanding chronic/semi-chronic therapies, with deliberate entry into secularly growing infertility/IVF and biosimilars.
scores.quote: deepens our footprint in the rapidly growing infertility market

scores.rationale: Net cash surplus with acquisitions confined to small complementary brand bolt-ons funded from internal accruals — management explicitly declined incremental investment for the export push.
scores.quote: internal we have enough cash generated from the business… We are a net cash surplus company

scores.rationale: 21-year build with sustained outperformance — five IPM rank positions gained in three years and repeated delivery ahead of the 15%/20% guidance (FY26: 17% revenue, 33% PAT).
scores.quote: in fact ahead of our guided range of 15% revenue growth and 20% PAT growth. Our revenue for FY26 grew at 17% while PAT increased by 33%

scores.rationale: Only listed in Dec 2025 after two decades of building quietly in a middle-of-pyramid niche, with humility written into the stated culture — though the maiden calls carry noticeable self-promotion.
scores.quote: We believe in internal promotion, adaptability and humbleness

scores.rationale: Internal promotion is an explicit cultural pillar, training spend rose 50%, and the bench is visible — new President (India Business), VP Corporate Strategy, plus two new divisions and an IVF taskforce staffed in Q4.
scores.quote: Investing in employee training increased by 50%

scores.rationale: Owns and explains the Q4 margin decline attributing it to specific growth investments, and answers the primary-vs-secondary sales discrepancy directly rather than deflecting; candour is stated as a value but the track record post-listing is short.
scores.quote: Decline was on account of an increase in employee cost with respect to the addition of two new divisions

scores.rationale: Strong headline results are inflated by acquisitions and a one-time labour-code adjustment, and with only three post-IPO calls there is insufficient independently verifiable history to separate managerial skill from a favourable IPM upcycle.
scores.quote: Adjusted profit after tax, excluding the impact on account of one-time labor code changes

scores.rationale: Brands hold respectable but not monopoly-like positions — top-five in categories and #2 in povidone iodine — with no evidence of owning a category in the prescriber's mind.
scores.quote: many of other brands ranking amongst top five in the respective categories

scores.rationale: Chronic/semi-chronic concentration (72% of revenue) creates real prescription-level switching costs and repeat scripts, though nothing approaching a regional or captive monopoly.
scores.quote: driven by improved prescription stickiness, better patient compliance

scores.rationale: Indian branded formulations is a fragmented market where CORONA ranks only 27th with roughly 1% share — the opposite of a stable oligopoly.
scores.quote: Our industry ranking has improved to 27th position

scores.rationale: Branded generics has low structural entry barriers with dozens of credible players; CORONA's own defences are GMP accreditations and brand equity rather than industry-level barriers, and pricing power is evidently weak given growth comes from volume not price.
scores.quote: we are number one fastest growing pharmaceutical Company amongst top 30 pharma companies in India

scores.rationale: MNCs and larger Indian players are actively divesting brands into CORONA's hands — Bayer/Zydus and Wockhardt in FY26 alone, following GSK, Abbott and Sanofi — a repeatable supply of donated share.
scores.quote: After acquiring brands from giants like GlaxoSmithKline, Abbott, Sanofi, etc., we have been successful in scaling those brands considerably

scores.rationale: Deliberate middle-of-pyramid, semi-urban positioning that larger players under-serve, though listing in Dec 2025 and coverage by JM, IIFL and Ambit is rapidly removing the obscurity.
scores.quote: CORONA adopts a differentiated strategy focused on the middle of pyramid

scores.rationale: Brand equity is real (70+ brands, 38 above INR 10cr, two above INR 100cr) and EBITDA margin improved 80bps to 20.9%, but pricing power is limited since growth is volume/NI-led rather than price-led.
scores.quote: two of our brands have surpassed the INR 100 crore revenue milestone

scores.rationale: Positions on quality credentials — EU GMP, WHO GMP and now EAEU GMP plus backward-integrated hormone API supply — which is what specialist prescribers buy, though this is table stakes among credible IPM players.
scores.quote: Both facilities are WHO GMP certified. Additionally, our Gujarat facility is also EU GMP certified

scores.rationale: The core asset is field-force intimacy — a pan-India MR network targeting specialists and super-specialists, expanded in Q4FY26 with two new divisions and an IVF taskforce at the cost of near-term margin.
scores.quote: Our pan-India presence supported by an expanding network of distributors and medical representatives enables deeper engagement with medical profession

scores.rationale: Correctly matched to a prescriber-intermediated retail model — brand equity plus intensive MR relationships with specialists rather than a corporate TCO pitch.
scores.quote: intensifying our focus with specialist and super-specialist prescribers through our medical representative network

scores.rationale: Capability is being added — two DSIR-approved R&D centres, hormone API backward integration and three biosimilar launches — but this is formulation/line-extension work, not a deep multi-product technology edge.
scores.quote: We also have marked our entry into the biosimilars and biologics market with the launch of three biosimilar products in FY26

scores.rationale: No two-sided network exists in the business model and none is claimed across the three calls; growth comes from field-force reach and brand acquisition, which do not self-reinforce with scale.
Distribution and MR reach is the company's genuine competitive engine and is being deepened, but at 27th in IPM it is not a reach rivals cannot match — the larger IPM players have wider networks.
scores.quote: By strengthening our field force in these markets and maintaining a clear focus on specialist and super specialist, CORONA is well positioned to capture value in the middle of the pyramid

scores.rationale: Capacity was expanded from 1.5m to 2.5m units/month within FY26 plus new housing/enclosure, lens and cable lines, funded from internal accruals, while EBITDA margin expanded 540bps for the year and 800bps in Q4 — clear high-return growth capex, not maintenance.
scores.quote: Our manufacturing capacity has now reached 2.5 million units... The project is fully funded through internal accruals.

scores.rationale: Sustained A&P — celebrity endorsement (Vijay Sethupathi), cricket series, IFSEC, PACC title sponsorship, airport outdoor — is tied directly to the brand mix that management repeatedly cites as a margin driver, with CP PLUS brand at 86-87% of revenue.
scores.quote: margin improving by 391 basis points to 12.6%, primarily due to favorable product and brand mix

scores.rationale: R&D spend is visibly rising (Noida, Ahmedabad, Taiwan subsidiary, upcoming Bangalore, DSIR-certified labs) and has already yielded the largest STQC-certified portfolio and a shift of the portfolio to 73-75% higher-value IP products.
scores.quote: IP products made up 73% of CP PLUS portfolio, underscoring the sustained shift towards higher value IP solutions

scores.rationale: M&A is small, complementary and vertical — buying out Dixon's 50% of the manufacturing JV (accretive in H1 FY26) plus an Orient Cables JV for captive cable supply — no large or unrelated deals.
scores.quote: our consolidation of the subsidiary AIL Dixon is showing gains in H1 FY26

scores.rationale: No buyback, dividend or distribution policy is discussed in any of the four calls; IPO proceeds were applied to debt repayment rather than returns.

The business is deliberately becoming more asset-heavy through backward integration (housing/moulding, lens assembly, cable JV, further land acquisition), offset by strong operating leverage and a brand/distribution moat — no explicit turnover disclosure to judge either way.
scores.quote: we are also evaluating further land acquisition opportunities in the North of India

scores.rationale: Documented share capture from 20.8% in FY25 to ~45.4% by Q3 FY26, far exceeding the company's own IPO projection of ~36%, with further runway via the new Eyra/Nexivue brands into the unorganized segment.
scores.quote: As of Q3 FY 2026, our market share reached approximately 45.4%

scores.rationale: Overseas presence is an R&D subsidiary in Taiwan and aspirational 'building in India for the world' language, with revenue growth described as coming from Indian geographies — no executed international commercial expansion in the window.
scores.quote: proudly building in India for the world

scores.rationale: Growth was explicitly volume- and share-led through H1 with no price rises, but mix (analog to IP, own-brand to 86-87%) is a stated margin driver and a 6-8% price hike was passed through in January 2026 with more planned.
scores.quote: We have also announced a price hike of 6% to 8% in the month of January 2026, which is already passed to the market

scores.rationale: The company sits mid-upcycle on demand rather than near a bottom, and the input cycle is running against it — semiconductor, DDR, flash and sensor costs are said to keep rising until 2027.
scores.quote: Industry trends indicate that costs are likely to continue rising until 2027.

scores.rationale: The Indian video surveillance end market is in secular expansion — Rs106bn in FY25 growing at a 16.5% CAGR to FY30 with units rising from 39.7m to ~75m, driven by urbanization, safe-city spend and the analog-to-IP/AI shift.
scores.quote: The growth is expected to continue at a CAGR of 16.5% annually until FY '30.

scores.rationale: Growth is organic and internally funded, IPO proceeds went to deleveraging with finance costs down 38%, and expansion is via small JVs/partnerships rather than large M&A.
scores.quote: Most of this has been funded entirely through internal accruals.

scores.rationale: A consistent long-horizon localization agenda — 2017 Dixon manufacturing JV, buyout in 2024, backward integration into housings, lenses and cables, and co-designing India's first indigenous vision SoC with L&T Semiconductor — shows independent, tenacious execution ahead of the regulatory shift.
scores.quote: Together, we are co-designing India's first IPC SoC with Vision AI technology

scores.rationale: Management communicates plainly and operationally, but the company is freshly listed, guidance-forward and runs deliberately high-profile celebrity and sponsorship campaigns, so it is not a low-limelight profile.
scores.quote: our new brand campaign featuring Tamil Nadu superstar Vijay Sethupathi

scores.rationale: Evidence of systematic capability building — 4,100+ employees, 50,000 participants trained under Mission Tech with the Ministry of Skill Development, and rapid hiring of 20-year global R&D talent — though no explicit internal succession pipeline is described beyond the promoter family.
scores.quote: successfully engaged over 50,000 participants until now under our Mission Tech and other training programs

scores.rationale: Management disclosed the Q1 STQC supply-chain disruption, the Rs7.7cr one-time labour-code provision, and openly tempered expectations on lens localization economics, while setting and then beating explicit guidance.
scores.quote: initially I don't see major margin impact because there will be a sustenance period of learning curve

scores.rationale: The extraordinary results are substantially a regulatory windfall — STQC certification displacing Chinese brands — so share going 20.8% to 45.4% and margin 12% to 18% cannot yet be cleanly attributed to management skill alone.
scores.quote: assuming a meaningful consolidation of the Chinese players' market share among the Indian manufacturers

scores.rationale: CP PLUS holds a strong mind-share position as the first true consumer brand in Indian surveillance with the widest certified portfolio, though at ~45% it is a dominant leader rather than a true monopoly and services/aftermarket monetization is still nascent.
scores.quote: the first player to create a true consumer brand in India's security and surveillance industry

scores.rationale: STQC certification, cyber-secure requirements and the installed CP PLUS ecosystem (cloud, analytics, OnVigil, full bill-of-material under one brand) create real but moderate switching friction for SIs and enterprise customers.
scores.quote: supporting products for providing complete bill of material under the CP PLUS brand to our customers

scores.rationale: The market is consolidating post-STQC toward a handful of certified Indian and MNC brands, and component shortages are squeezing smaller players further, but the channel still runs through 1,000+ distributors with some negotiating power.
scores.quote: While this may sound disruptive for smaller players, it also will lead to supply consolidation

scores.rationale: STQC certification, localization depth and scale manufacturing are hard entry barriers, and pricing has been rational — an industry-wide 6-8% hike was passed through rather than discounted away, with stable promoter ownership plus Dixon retaining 6.6%.
scores.quote: Some of the brands are still grappling in the process of certification.

scores.rationale: There is an unusually large pool of weak donors — Chinese brands losing certified access, uncertified players stuck in backlog, and an unorganized interiors segment that the new Nexivue brand is explicitly built to take.
scores.quote: Nexiview targets the Indian interiors market, and aims to organize the unstructured segment

scores.rationale: The opposite of obscure — a freshly listed leader covered by ICICI and Axis, running mass-media celebrity campaigns and cricket sponsorships in a sector attracting heavy policy and capital attention.
scores.quote: high-impact visibility across Indian cricket series, and outdoor campaign across major airports

scores.rationale: Brand recall is a stated USP in the consumer segment and the company demonstrated pricing power by passing a 6-8% hike straight through, with FY26 EBITDA margin reaching 13.7% and 18% in Q4.
scores.quote: the strong brand recall of CP PLUS is a big USP

scores.rationale: The purchase decision has shifted decisively to certified, cyber-secure, trusted-source product across government, BFSI and enterprise buyers — reliability and compliance ahead of price.
scores.quote: notable shift towards cyber-security certified, domestic Indian brands

scores.rationale: Distribution and service reach are exceptional — 1,000+ distributors, 2,000+ system integrators, 500+ cities, 48 branches, 13 RMA centres, franchisee Galaxy stores and expanding feet-on-street to consultants and architects.
scores.quote: over 1,000 plus distributors and 2,000 plus system integrators across more than 500 cities

scores.rationale: The benefit mix is well matched by customer type — brand and touch-and-feel retail for the 10% home segment, certified reliability and vertical feet-on-street for the 30% enterprise/government book, with 60% SMB served on brand plus availability.
scores.quote: Our largest pie comes from the SMB space, which constitutes 60% of our revenue

scores.rationale: Genuine and widening technical depth (multi-SoC architecture across six non-Chinese vendors, Qualcomm edge-AI partnership, indigenous vision SoC with L&T, AI analytics), but the core silicon edge is partner-derived rather than proprietary today.
scores.quote: we have proactively adopted a multi-SoC product strategy

scores.rationale: No self-reinforcing two-sided network is evident — the moat is brand, certification and distribution; cloud and OnVigil are attached services rather than a network that strengthens with each added user.
scores.quote: CP PLUS Cloud Storage for redundancy backup and mobile-accessible video storage

scores.rationale: The distribution and after-sales footprint — 1,000+ distributors, 2,000+ SIs, 500+ cities, 48 branch offices and 13 RMA service centres — is the scale advantage rivals cannot replicate in a category where installation and service matter.
scores.quote: CP PLUS has the largest distribution network

scores.rationale: Capex is clearly growth-led (Kothavadi phase-I, Hosur/Shoolagiri alloy wheel plants, INR280cr DR Axion expansion on a larger land parcel) with a stated ROCE screen, but returns are still unproven — consolidated pre-tax ROCE was only 14-15% with start-up cash losses at Kothavadi and Shoolagiri.
scores.quote: we are announcing the CAPEX, and we check on the return of capital employed, and the viability of such a project

scores.rationale: No mention of advertising or brand promotion spend in any of the four calls — it is a B2B tier-1 supplier.
The calls discuss customer part development and validation timelines but never R&D spend, R&D intensity or R&D-driven new-product economics.

Sunbeam was a large, distressed, complex acquisition — not a strong bolt-on — requiring plant closure, union settlement, modernisation of obsolete equipment and customer exits, and it is still only single-digit EBITDA margin a year later.
scores.quote: We are just lacking behind on the margin-wise with a single, still at single-digit for various reasons. We are on the right track that we are exiting customers where it's not profitable

scores.rationale: No discussion of dividends or buybacks in the window; the only capital-structure reference is the QIP equity raise, which speaks to funding rather than distribution policy.
This is a capital-intensive foundry/machining business — repeated large capex, net debt/EBITDA of 2.27-2.87x, and pre-tax ROCE of only 14-15% — the opposite of asset-light.
scores.quote: ROCE pre-tax annualized is 14%. Still the plants are not fully operational

scores.rationale: Management points to a subscale Indian aluminium tier-1 base versus 3-4x larger global peers, rising export enquiries and OEMs outsourcing in-house machining — genuine runway plus evidence of order wins ramping.
scores.quote: the aluminum products segment is still subscale in India overall whereas the global tier 1, tier 2 companies, the magnitude of those companies are at least 3x, 4x of the Indian tier 1 suppliers today

scores.rationale: Credible multi-location expansion — Fronberg Guss in Germany used as a technology and development base, new Indian plants at Hosur/Shoolagiri/Bhiwadi/Gujarat, and rising Europe/North America export enquiries — though it is capacity footprint, not a travelling premium brand.
scores.quote: We are getting inquiries for 4-wheelers for export market. Both Europe and North America, we are increasing

scores.rationale: Deliberate mix shift toward machined/value-added parts, higher-horsepower tractor and heavy-duty CV content, and active resetting of legacy prices, though a meaningful part of reported topline is commodity aluminium pass-through rather than real price.
scores.quote: we are focusing on value-added products like casting and machining. We are not interested really to do only the casting portion

scores.rationale: The CV cycle is described as muted with green shoots and tractors already recovering, positioning the powertrain segment near a cyclical trough with an identifiable content-per-vehicle upturn ahead.
scores.quote: tractor is doing very well in this financial year and commercial vehicle is showing green shoots of some marginal growth

scores.rationale: The stationary-engine/Kothavadi programme is levered to data-centre and AI power demand, with a fully booked first $100m order book, global capacity sold out and a possible phase-2 — a genuinely secular end market.
scores.quote: the data center market or AI is booming all over the world... Capacity-wise, almost everybody is full

scores.rationale: Deleveraging and ROCE-gated capex are positives, but the recent record is defined by large inorganic bets (Sunbeam, DR Axion, Fronberg), a QIP raise and standalone net debt/EBITDA of 2.87x — not an organic, low-leverage steward profile.
scores.quote: In the stand-alone net debt to EBITDA is around 2.87 because we have borrowed in Craftsman for the acquisitions

scores.rationale: Evidence of a decade-long horizon executed independently — the stationary-engine opportunity studied since 2020, Fronberg bought to acquire the technology first-hand, three years of pre-emptive automation investment, and the grinding Sunbeam restructuring pushed through.
scores.quote: our thorough study from 2020 and careful understanding of the project and customers and also the acquisition of Fronberg, which has allowed us to have a first-hand view of the technology

scores.rationale: Calls are notably terse and unpromotional — the CMD opens two of the four by pointing to the uploaded presentation and going straight to Q&A rather than delivering a narrative.
scores.quote: We have uploaded the presentation. I hope all of you had a chance to have a look at it. So straight away, we can start with the Q&A.

scores.rationale: Beyond labour settlement, headcount reduction and India-Germany team collaboration, there is no discussion of talent development or leadership pipeline.

Consistently owns shortfalls without spin — cash losses at Kothavadi, alloy wheel margins below even high single digits, Sunbeam still lagging, unviable legacy business needing 'tough decisions' — and gives caveated guidance rather than a headline number.
scores.quote: we are not in the double-digit margin yet or even high single digit. We are lower than that

scores.rationale: Headline growth (H1 sales INR3,786cr vs INR2,365cr) is largely consolidation of acquisitions plus aluminium price inflation rather than demonstrated per-unit skill, though the Sunbeam turnaround and order wins are real operational achievements — the two roughly offset.
scores.quote: If there's any change in aluminum prices, there can be some commodity price impact which will either inflate or deflate the top line

scores.rationale: In large stationary-engine castings the company benefits from a scarcity position — no new global capacity being added and everyone full — which approximates a niche monopoly-like standing, but not in the broader auto-component business.
scores.quote: owing to the no new capacities coming up anywhere in the world in general, because we started this a little earlier, we got some head start

scores.rationale: Three-to-four-year development and validation cycles, customer-mandated prove-outs in Germany, dedicated tooling and BIS approvals create real switching costs once a part is homologated.
scores.quote: the lead time for development of these products and validation of the products is three to four years' time

scores.rationale: The customer set is a handful of powerful OEMs that hold the negotiating power — evidenced by legacy prices that must be renegotiated and pass-throughs that lag by a month or two — not an industry where the end customer lacks leverage.
scores.quote: we have a pass-through with the customer. Some are immediate. Some are taking a month or two

scores.rationale: High barriers in complex castings (no new world capacity, capital and validation intensity) sit alongside evidently irrational pricing in low-value work, where Craftsman is exiting customers and refusing supply because economics do not clear.
scores.quote: Where aluminum price pass-through is not there, then we are declining to supply

scores.rationale: Weak players exist to take share from — Sunbeam itself was one before acquisition, Indian tier-1 aluminium suppliers are subscale, and OEMs are donating in-house machining volumes to outsourcing.
scores.quote: There is a shift towards outsourcing of machining activity, which the OEMs are doing in-house

scores.rationale: The stationary-engine casting niche is genuinely under-served by new capital, but the company itself is a well-covered listed midcap fielding questions from multiple institutional brokerages each quarter.
scores.quote: no new capacities coming up anywhere in the world

scores.rationale: There is no image- or taste-driven pricing power; margins are explicitly commodity-linked with optical compression from aluminium and energy inflation, and the only pricing lever is refusing unprofitable supply.
scores.quote: aluminum per se, the commodity prices are going up, energy prices are going up, labor cost is going up... The margins on basic raw casting is not going to be viable

scores.rationale: Customers buy certainty — new entrants visited Fronberg, gained confidence and mandated that development be completed in Germany before transfer, and management frames the coming CV product cycle as demanding supplier reliability above price.
scores.quote: they expressed a lot of confidence in Fronberg after visiting them... And they have mandated that we complete the development in Germany before we shift it

scores.rationale: Proximity to customer clusters is a deliberate advantage — plants positioned across Chennai (the emerging automotive hub), Hosur, Bhiwadi and Gujarat to sit close to OEM demand.
scores.quote: we are strategically placed in many geographic locations for the business

scores.rationale: The customer base is purely corporate/OEM and the benefit stack matches it correctly — reliability, capability and TCO (productivity, fuel efficiency) plus multi-year validation lock-in rather than consumer intangibles.
scores.quote: they are only battling with the delta cost, rather the productivity and fuel efficiency are offsetting the initial investment

scores.rationale: There is a real process-technology edge in complex castings and machining — Fronberg's know-how, joint India-Germany prove-outs, and three years of automation investment ahead of the new Labour Code — but it is process capability, not multi-product R&D depth.
scores.quote: Craftsman has been preparing very well for the last 3 years on manpower productivity by investment into automation and better equipment

scores.rationale: A contract manufacturer of castings and machined components to a concentrated OEM base has no two-sided network dynamic, and none is claimed anywhere in the calls.
Sales are direct to a small number of OEMs with multi-plant proximity as the only reach advantage; there is no distribution or service network rivals could not replicate.
scores.quote: we don't really worry about which is the customer

scores.rationale: Asset-light AMC is investing modestly but steadily for growth — branches up from 23 to 29 in FY26 with a stated 3-5 per year cadence plus continuing digital platform spend, though no ROIC quantification is given.
scores.quote: we've grown our branches to 29 branches from 23 of last year

scores.rationale: No A&P or brand-spend disclosure in any of the four calls.
Only a generic mention of investing in the investment/research team, with a deliberately low product cadence of one to two launches a year and no evidence of R&D efficiency.
scores.quote: investments in the investment team and research capability

scores.rationale: No acquisitions discussed in the last-12-months calls.
No dividend, buyback or distribution-policy commentary in the excerpts (company listed only in Oct 2025).

Structurally asset-light — FY26 revenue of INR424.9 crores on a business whose main balance-sheet item is a ~INR650 crore investment book, with cost-to-income held under 40% — but the moat protecting it is weak in a 52-AMC field.
scores.quote: Our cost-to-income ratio for us -- we like it to be below 40

scores.rationale: CRAMC is losing share, not gaining: closing AUM grew 3.2% YoY in FY26 versus ~21% industry QAAUM growth, and Q1 FY27 QAAUM grew 7% versus industry 10.5%.
scores.quote: our closing AUM stands at approximately INR1.07 lakh crores, up by almost 3.2% year-on-year

scores.rationale: Expansion is purely domestic penetration (B30 at ~24% of AUM, 29 branches); overseas/GIFT City remains only an option under evaluation with no execution yet.
scores.quote: whether we should do AIFs, whether we should get into, say, GIFT City or passives

scores.rationale: Yields rose ~3bps but management attributes it largely to the mechanical TER slab structure after a market downturn rather than pricing power, and the stated 35-38bps comfort band implies willingness to dilute yield for AUM.
scores.quote: the yields are based on the TER slab structure... the market had taken a downturn which resulted in higher TERs

scores.rationale: As a 91%-equity fund house, it enters FY27 just after a ~15% Nifty correction with the index recovering 7% in Q1 FY27 — a plausible post-trough position for mark-to-market AUM.
scores.quote: NIFTY correcting approximately 15% during this period

scores.rationale: The Indian MF end-market is in clear secular expansion — industry AUM up ~18-21% YoY through FY26 and monthly SIP flows hitting an all-time high above INR32,000 crores.
scores.quote: monthly inflows crossing the INR32,000 crores for the industry in March 2026, which is an all-time high

scores.rationale: Consistently organic and restrained — no M&A, one-or-two NFOs a year, refusal to chase cyclical commodity/index fads, and an explicit cost-to-income guardrail.
scores.quote: We generally do one or two products a year. We don't believe in launching multiple products.

scores.rationale: Management defends a long-horizon active, mutual-fund-only core against repeated investor pressure to launch ETFs/commodity/global funds, though it has been slow rather than tenacious in adjacent segments.
scores.quote: These are cyclical products... We like to be in a category which can outperform over a longer period of time

scores.rationale: Low-key, substance-first tone across the maiden and subsequent calls — no promotional framing, MD routinely deflects questions to the CFO/heads and describes the business plainly.
scores.quote: to me, if it's a relatively simple business, you got to keep it simple

scores.rationale: Only indirect evidence — investment in the investment/research team and Gaurav Goyal's internal progression from Head of Sales to Chief Business Officer across the four calls — with no articulated talent-development system.
scores.quote: MR. GAURAV GOYAL – CHIEF BUSINESS OFFICER

scores.rationale: Notably candid — separately disclosed the INR10.15 crore one-time employee/IPO expense and adjusted PBT, admitted growth was running below the 30% medium-term aspiration, and openly called the industry commoditized.
scores.quote: ours is a commoditized business in more ways than one

scores.rationale: Reported strength flatters the underlying business: Q1 FY27 revenue +20% and PAT +24% owe much to a mechanically higher TER slab and market beta while AUM growth trailed the industry, so results overstate skill.
scores.quote: Profit after tax stood at INR75 crores, registering 24% year-on-year growth

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like position anywhere — 52 AMCs sell regulator-mandated identical product categories and any innovation is copyable.
scores.quote: the regulator expects you to have the same, kind of, product... it can always be copied by the industry

scores.rationale: Switching costs are minimal in mutual funds; the only stickiness is the ~21 lakh SIP book contributing ~INR755-768 crores a month, which is habit rather than lock-in.
scores.quote: over 21 lakh active SIP accounts, with monthly contributions from SIP and STP combined of INR755 crores

scores.rationale: The industry is fragmented, not a stable oligopoly — 52 AMCs compete and CRAMC's ~INR1.2 lakh crores is barely 1.5% of the INR82.2 lakh crore industry.
scores.quote: there are, sir, 52 AMC, which provide the same commodity-type business

scores.rationale: Regulation provides some entry friction but also caps pricing via TER slabs and forces product uniformity, and management concedes rising compliance costs with no pricing rationality advantage.
scores.quote: there is rising costs of compliance within the regulatory framework

scores.rationale: No identified weak rivals to feed on; on the evidence CRAMC is itself the donor, growing AUM well below the industry rate through FY26.
scores.quote: Quarterly average AUM increased by 7% year-on-year

scores.rationale: A modest, unflashy franchise, but the Indian AMC space is a heavily analysed, capital-attracting sector and the company has just listed onto public markets with quarterly analyst scrutiny.
scores.quote: it is our first analyst call post our listing on the 16th of October

scores.rationale: Trust and a three-decade Canara Bank-Robeco pedigree are cited as the real differentiator, supporting mid-band yields of 35-38bps and high operating margins, though not genuine pricing power.
scores.quote: your true differentiator will be the trust you're able to build with your investors and performance over time

scores.rationale: The proposition is explicitly reliability-led — consistent risk-adjusted performance and service to both investors and distributors rather than lowest cost.
scores.quote: Performance and the way you service your clients, both investors as well as distributors

scores.rationale: Distribution reach is being actively widened — empanelled partners up from ~53,955 to 56,890 in four quarters, 29 branches, plus growing digital platform adoption.
scores.quote: Distribution network expanded to over 56,890 empaneled partners

scores.rationale: The base is well matched to a trust/brand-led retail proposition — ~86% individual investors and 50.8 lakh folios, with only 14% institutional money.
scores.quote: Individual investors contributed 86% of our AUM, while institutional investors accounted for 14%

scores.rationale: Digital platforms are described only as efficiency and engagement tools, with no proprietary technology edge in a business management itself calls copyable.
scores.quote: increasing adoption of our digital platforms, enabling seamless investor engagement... driving operational efficiencies

scores.rationale: No two-sided network dynamic exists — scale brings TER-slab yield compression rather than a self-reinforcing advantage.
scores.quote: the yields are based on the TER slab structure, which is related to the AUM of the company

scores.rationale: A real but unremarkable reach — ~56,000 partners and 29 branches added at 3-5 a year — that larger AMCs comfortably match, and it has not translated into share gains.
scores.quote: we have roughly opened about 5 new branches per year

scores.rationale: Genuine growth investment in distribution and digital during a downturn — 183 branches added in FY26 and 42 more in Q1 FY27 to 2,276 branches across 457 districts, plus the Grameen Mahi app build-out, though incremental ROIC is still recovering (FY26 ROE 10.7%).
scores.quote: We opened 183 branches to close with 2,236 branches by March 2026

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend in any of the four calls.
No R&D spend or R&D-driven product pipeline is discussed; digital app work is described operationally, not as an R&D program.
No acquisitions were made or discussed in the last twelve months, so there is no deal record to judge.
Calls discuss capital adequacy (24.9%) and internal-accrual funding of growth but contain no dividend or buyback policy discussion.
As a balance-sheet lender the business is structurally asset-heavy — growth requires capital and 3.0x debt-equity leverage — so asset turnover is inherently low despite the moat in distribution.
scores.quote: total equity at INR 7,842 Crore and a debt equity ratio at a conservative 3.0x

scores.rationale: Clear share capture during a sector shakeout — 9.8 lakh borrowers added in FY26 and AUM up 16.4% YoY while the industry deleveraged — with a large stated runway (23.5 crore low-to-middle income households), tempered by CAGL already being the largest NBFC-MFI.
scores.quote: We continue to scale borrower acquisition with 3.3 Lakh borrowers added in Q4, while 9.8 Lakh borrowers added in FY26

scores.rationale: Well-executed domestic diversification away from concentration risk — half of new borrowers came from outside the top three states and the network now spans 457 districts — but this is within-India expansion, not a premium brand travelling abroad.
scores.quote: we added 2.1 Lakh borrowers in Q3 FY26 and 6.4 Lakh during the 9-months FY26 period, of which 50% came outside of the top three states

scores.rationale: Growth is overwhelmingly volume-led (~1 lakh new borrowers per month is the stated primary driver) and management is contemplating cutting prices, with only mix (retail finance to 20.6%) working in its favour.
scores.quote: accordingly take a call on passing the pricing benefit to the customers in H2 FY27

scores.rationale: The company is sitting exactly at the bottom-to-upturn transition of the MFI credit cycle — PAR 15 accretion fell from 47 bps (Sep-25) to ~15 bps (Q1 FY27) and PAT went from INR 126 Crore to INR 493 Crore across the four calls.
scores.quote: Q4 FY26 marks a decisive inflection in our performance trajectory

scores.rationale: Underpenetrated rural/semi-urban micro-retail credit is described as growing double-digit with a 23.5 crore household target market, though the last two years showed this end-market is cyclically fragile rather than smoothly secular.
scores.quote: India's rural and semi-urban micro retail credit market across segments is growing at double-digit rates

scores.rationale: Purely organic growth, conservative 3.0x leverage and 24.9% CRAR, self-funded via internal accruals, and counter-cyclical investment (branches, hiring, audit frequency raised) precisely through the worst of the credit cycle.
scores.quote: net worth increased from INR 2,734 Crore in FY20 to INR 8,347 Crore in Q1 FY27, compounding at 20% CAGR, of which 86% increase came just through internal accruals

scores.rationale: Management held to a long-term mission through demonetisation, COVID and the MFI cycle and has set a public CY2028 INR 50,000 Crore AUM target, but tenacity is somewhat offset by repeatedly revised credit-cost guidance within the year.
scores.quote: Over the past two years, we were navigating one of the most challenging environments. We continued to work on the future and never lost sight of our long-term mission.

scores.rationale: Calls are led by operating metrics and sequencing of priorities rather than personality or promotion, with the sole leadership announcement being a factual note on the new independent Chairman.
scores.quote: We prioritized collections first, then portfolio maintenance and only then growth.

scores.rationale: Attrition was systematically driven down from 35.2% to 20.6% through training, front-line leadership and proactive salary restructuring ahead of the new labour codes, and the CEO was promoted internally to MD.
scores.quote: employee attrition continued to moderate meaningfully, standing at 20.6% as of Q1 FY27 against 25.8% in Q1 FY26

scores.rationale: Management pre-announced its own guidance misses in detail (70-100 bps FY26 credit-cost deviation, FY26 ending at 6.74% vs 5.5-6.0% guided), quantified each driver, and plainly labelled the period difficult rather than spinning it.
scores.quote: our credit cost ended at 6.74% as against the guidance of 5.5% to 6.0%

scores.rationale: The dazzling recent numbers (ROE 24.4%, PAT +720% YoY) are largely a cyclical rebound off a written-off base — 7.6% of the book was written off in FY26 — so results here overstate incremental skill and warrant discounting.
scores.quote: our Q1 FY27 PAT grew 720% YoY to INR 493 Crore, resulting in an ROA of 5.9% and ROE of 24.4%

scores.rationale: No monopoly position in the borrower's mind — customers routinely hold multiple lender relationships and CAGL competes on being the lowest-cost lender rather than the only option.
scores.quote: GLP % of borrowers with > 3 lenders at 6.9% in Sep-25 vs. 25.3% in Aug-24

scores.rationale: Switching costs are low in group microfinance, but long vintage and lifecycle graduation create partial lock-in — Unnati borrowers average 7.7 years of relationship before moving to higher-ticket products.
scores.quote: our Unnati loan customers carry an average vintage of 7.7 years and an average credit score of 732

scores.rationale: Microfinance is a fragmented field of NBFC-MFIs, SFBs and banks all lending to the same households, with regulators rather than industry structure imposing discipline.
scores.quote: PAR 15+ in case of borrowers with 4 lenders stood at 15.1% as of mid-Sep 25

scores.rationale: MFIN guardrails have forced sector-wide deleveraging and rational underwriting over six quarters, and CAGL's risk-based pricing plus 8.9% marginal funding cost is a barrier weaker entrants cannot match.
scores.quote: The implementation of MFIN guardrails has meaningfully strengthened the overall quality of the microfinance ecosystem.

scores.rationale: The credit cycle has left weakened competitors from whom CAGL is visibly taking share, funded by a structural cost-of-borrowing advantage that fell 60 bps to 9.2% during a year when peers were capital-constrained.
scores.quote: we continue to leverage our risk-based pricing strategy, low cost of borrowings, and efficient operating structure to protect our ROA within the 4–4.5% range, whilst being one of the lowest-cost lender in the industry

scores.rationale: This is a heavily covered listed name — the four calls alone were hosted by Motilal Oswal, HDFC, ICICI and Equirus with Nomura on the line — so it is neither ignored by capital nor under the radar.
scores.quote: hosted by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Limited

scores.rationale: Pricing is set by risk and regulation rather than image, and management is explicitly weighing rate cuts to customers as credit costs normalise — the opposite of image-derived pricing power.
scores.quote: take a call on passing the pricing benefit to the customers in H2 FY27, in line with the board-approved pricing policy

scores.rationale: Borrowers value assured, continuous credit access through cycles from a lender that stayed on the ground when others pulled back, and management explicitly leans on that trust to cross-sell.
scores.quote: leveraging the trust our brand has built on the ground

scores.rationale: Accessibility is the core proposition — 2,276 branches across 457 districts with ~22,000 field staff, now paired with 15.4 lakh customers on the Grameen Mahi app driving 24.2% digital collections.
scores.quote: The accelerators behind this engine are formidable, vast distribution reach, dedicated foot on the street, localized intelligence

scores.rationale: The customer base is retail rural households and the benefit offered is correctly matched to convenience and lifecycle deepening rather than corporate TCO, with graduation into secured products building genuine stickiness.
scores.quote: We are building the capability to be the financial life cycle partner of the entire household across income stages, credit needs and life events.

scores.rationale: Grameen Mahi is a competent, well-adopted customer app (34.5% of borrowers) with real-time audit analytics behind it, but it is table-stakes digital execution rather than a deep multi-product technology edge.
scores.quote: taking our overall active base to 15.4 Lakh customers and 34.5% of our total borrower base

scores.rationale: Growth comes from branch openings and feet-on-street acquisition, not from any self-reinforcing two-sided network; the app is a one-sided customer channel.
scores.quote: We are strengthening our acquisition engines through three channels: group-based sourcing, individual lending and digital through the Grameen Mahi app.

scores.rationale: The clearest moat in the business — a rural branch and field network rivals cannot replicate, which is precisely what enabled collections-led survival of the credit cycle and now underpins cross-sell of retail products.
scores.quote: We opened 42 new branches during the quarter, taking our total network to 2,276 branches, a growth of 7.7% YoY, spread across 457 districts

scores.rationale: Management repeatedly cites investment in digital infrastructure, information security and Gen-AI but gives no quantum, split of growth vs maintenance, or incremental-ROIC evidence in any of the four calls.
scores.quote: We continue to make significant investments in digital infrastructure, information security, and building a future-ready talent pool.

scores.rationale: Brand-building runs through franchise activity (India Outlook Conclave, Infrastructure Yearbook, thought-leadership reports) and a Jan-2025 unified rebrand, but no A&P spend or payback is quantified.
scores.quote: In January 2025, we rolled out a new brand identity, positioning our businesses under a cohesive brand identity

scores.rationale: Product development consistently converts into shipped offerings — Gen-AI credit assessment deployed for global clients and Gen-AI embedded into Credit+ ICON — though there is no disclosed R&D line or efficiency metric.
scores.quote: We integrated our Gen-AI capabilities into the credit assessment and credit solution, Credit + ICON, which we offer to our clients.

scores.rationale: Two small, simple, complementary bolt-ons in the window — Peter Lee Associates (Australia benchmarking) and PriceMetrix (Toronto wealth analytics) — each extending an existing franchise, though post-deal margin impact is never broken out.
scores.quote: completed the acquisition of PriceMetrix to deepen our presence in the wealth management space

scores.rationale: A steady, rising dividend policy (interim raised to INR9 from INR8) is evident, but no buyback and no valuation-linked distribution discipline is discussed.
scores.quote: the Board declared an interim dividend of INR9 per share in quarter 1 FY26 compared to INR8 per share in the same quarter last year

scores.rationale: The business is inherently asset-light — people and IP rather than plant ('5,000-plus experienced professionals', 'people are our biggest and most important IP') — paired with a rating/benchmarking franchise, though no turnover or ROIC figures are given on the calls.
scores.quote: People are our biggest and most important IP

scores.rationale: Explicit wallet-share ambition plus new logos and client-footprint expansion, but in the core Indian ratings business it is already the leader, limiting runway.
scores.quote: our focus remains sharp on increasing wallet share in our core markets and expanding into adjacencies, new client segments, and geographies

scores.rationale: Sustained, executed expansion across the window — Bogota delivery centre (2024), Canada entry with PriceMetrix (2026), West Asia client growth — now serving 11,400+ clients in 40 countries.
scores.quote: we've added a new geography, Canada, followed by our acquisition of PriceMetrix, a Toronto-based organization

scores.rationale: Growth is described as driven by issuance/bank-credit volumes, new logos and one-off timing/FX effects rather than price or mix, with the CFO flagging USD4.5m of Q1 FY26 revenue as a timing pull-forward.
scores.quote: the accelerated closure of renewals in one of our global businesses has led to incremental revenues of approximately USD4.5 million in quarter 1 FY26... this is largely a timing effect

scores.rationale: Management points to an identifiable credit upturn ahead — bank credit accelerating and bond issuance traction on easing policy — after a period of curtailed global discretionary spend.
scores.quote: Bank credit is likely to grow to 12%-13% just Fiscal, compared with 11-11.5% estimated for Fiscal 2025

scores.rationale: End markets are in secular expansion — private markets, sustainability/regulatory analytics, digital transformation and Gen-AI adoption by financial institutions, alongside India's deepening credit market.
scores.quote: the movement of capital to passive, alternative and private markets is opening up new avenues for data, analytics, and research

scores.rationale: Growth is predominantly organic with only small bolt-ons, no leverage discussion and continued investment through a weak global discretionary-spend cycle, though capital-allocation detail is thin.
scores.quote: profit before tax increased by 12.4% in full year 25, indicating disciplined cost management alongside continuing to invest in our growth agenda

scores.rationale: A 40-year franchise with a 20-year GAC partnership and consistent multi-year strategy shows tenacity, but genuine independence is limited by S&P Global control (S&P executives hold the chairmanship).
scores.quote: This year we are entering our 40th year of operations, and over that journey, we have continued to expand our strategic and analytical footprint both in India and globally.

scores.rationale: Management explicitly refuses quantitative guidance and segment-level detail, runs one annual analyst call led by business heads rather than a personality, with no celebrity framing.
scores.quote: As a policy, company refrains from giving specific quantitative guidance on its future performance.

scores.rationale: Systematic talent development plus a visibly working internal pipeline — Chhatwal moving Ratings MD to Group COO, Rai from Risk & Compliance to Ratings MD, Arora from CSO to Intelligence head — alongside six straight Great Place to Work certifications.
scores.quote: certified a Great Place to Work in India for the sixth consecutive year

scores.rationale: The CFO proactively separates underlying growth from FX gains and a revenue timing pull-forward and warns of normalisation, but disclosure policy blocks segment/contract detail and no material mistake is owned in the window.
scores.quote: As mentioned, this is largely a timing effect, and we expect this to normalize over the course of the rest of the year.

scores.rationale: The narrative is heavily award- and recognition-laden while the headline Q1 FY26 numbers are partly FX- and timing-flattered, so results cannot cleanly be attributed to skill on this evidence.

scores.rationale: CRISIL Ratings holds a mind-share monopoly with Indian bond investors, and Coalition Greenwich is the reference benchmark for global corporate and investment banks.
scores.quote: Crisil Ratings maintained its leadership in corporate bond ratings, given investor preference for best-in-class ratings

scores.rationale: Switching costs are real — regulator-mandated ratings with multi-year surveillance, delegated S&P surveillance work in GAC, and subscription benchmarking that loses comparability if dropped — though never quantified on the calls.
scores.quote: Crisil Global Analytical Center witnessed growth in delegation of surveillance from S&P Global Ratings

scores.rationale: Indian ratings is a stable, SEBI-licensed few-player oligopoly where issuers pay for investor acceptance rather than shop purely on price, but issuer-side fee negotiation still exists and is not addressed.
scores.quote: the two main drivers of the revenue pools for the rating agencies in India

scores.rationale: No new entrants are discussed across four calls, ownership is stable under S&P Global, and pricing is framed around quality preference rather than discounting — but pricing rationality is never explicitly addressed.
scores.quote: given investor preference for best-in-class ratings, and maintained healthy revenue growth during the quarter

scores.rationale: The repeated 'investor preference for best-in-class ratings' framing implies share migrating from weaker rating agencies, and new-logo wins in global research suggest displacement of sub-scale vendors, though competitors are never named.
scores.quote: the business added new logos during the quarter

scores.rationale: CRISIL is a high-profile, widely covered listed franchise that publicly markets its awards, brand and India Outlook seminars — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: we have been recognized as an iconic brand at the fifth edition of the Times Iconic Brand Conclave 2022

scores.rationale: The brand carries genuine image-driven pricing power in ratings and franchise publications, supported by robust margins, but the calls give no gross-margin or realisation data.
scores.quote: Our businesses have demonstrated resilience in 2024 and delivered revenue growth and robust margins in the first quarter.

scores.rationale: The entire proposition is certainty for mission-critical decisions — clients buy trust and analytical credibility, with price secondary, evidenced by rising NPS and blue-chip client roster.
scores.quote: helping financial institutions, governments, enterprises, and multilateral institutions make mission-critical decisions with confidence

scores.rationale: Deep client intimacy and accessibility via global delivery centres and a direct enterprise sales model, with rising net promoter score, though there is no consumer-style distribution advantage.

scores.rationale: The customer base is almost entirely corporate/institutional and the benefit offered matches it — reliability, regulatory compliance and embedded workflow lock-in rather than consumer intangibles.
scores.quote: We serve 11,400-plus clients in 40 countries globally, including India's leading banks, NBFCs, majority of the top AMCs, and most of the global corporate investment banks

scores.rationale: Credible applied-analytics and Gen-AI product edge validated by external ranking, but it is domain-led applied technology rather than a deep proprietary multi-product tech moat, and R&D intensity is undisclosed.
scores.quote: We were ranked number 20 and category leader in RiskTech AI 50 2025.

scores.rationale: The Coalition Greenwich benchmarking business has a genuine two-sided data network — banks contribute data to receive peer benchmarks, so value rises with participation — but this is one segment, not the whole company.
scores.quote: Crisil Coalition Greenwich witnessed some momentum in corporate and investment banking, with scaling of product offerings and client engagement, strengthening demand from large commercial banks.

scores.rationale: Reach across 40 countries with 11,400+ clients and multi-continent delivery centres (Bogota, India, Canada) is hard to replicate in India, but globally it is smaller than S&P/Moody's on the same channels.

scores.rationale: Genuinely asset-light with no capex programme disclosed; growth spend is routed through small acquisitions and a modest tech commitment rather than rising growth capex, so incremental ROIC on capex cannot be judged.
scores.quote: Our priority remains to reinvest in technology, key market and strategic opportunities

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend in any of the four calls.

A proprietary platform exists and drives operating leverage, but stated AI adoption is still nascent and the only quantified tech commitment is USD 2.5m spread over five years — no track record of R&D yielding new products yet.
scores.quote: We haven't used too much of AI as of today

scores.rationale: Four deals in one year (StudiesPlanet LATAM, 51% of Global Tree B2C, EduMentor, Medway NZ team) were individually small and complementary, but the pace is accelerating, one shifts the model toward B2C, and EBITDA margin fell from ~29% in Q1 to 23.19% in Q3 rather than improving post-deal.
scores.quote: FY 2026 was arguably our most active year in the inorganic front

scores.rationale: A first special interim dividend was declared in Q3 FY26 with distribution framed as a future intent; no buyback and no articulated policy yet.
scores.quote: This has also helped us in announcing our first special interim dividend today

scores.rationale: Commission-based, debt-free, minimal working capital and no proportional fixed-cost growth make this genuinely asset-light, though the protecting moat is qualified by 66% revenue concentration in ten university partners.
scores.quote: Our commission-based asset light model supports high margin and strong cash conversion... with minimal working capital need

scores.rationale: Share is under 1% of students sent to its own partner universities, with applications +43%, active agents +36% and university partners rising from ~170 to 400+ — large runway plus demonstrated capture.
scores.quote: our market share... it's less than 1%. Can this market share grow further? The answer is yes

scores.quote: we have set up a subsidiary of Crizac in UAE for our expansion into Middle East and Gulf countries

scores.rationale: Growth is predominantly volume-led (applications +43%, agents +36%) with only modest mix benefit — FY26 revenue +22.7% against enrollments +14% implies roughly 8% higher revenue per student, and applications grew three times faster than enrollments.
scores.quote: Application process grew 43% YoY... student enrollment grew 14% year-on-year

scores.rationale: US/Canada visa tightening redirects flows toward Crizac's UK/Ireland/NZ strongholds, but management also flags FX and geopolitical headwinds and Q4 growth decelerated to 15% — no clear cycle-bottom positioning with an identifiable upturn.
scores.quote: Canada and the United States have both tightened their immigration and study visa frameworks... redirecting demands to the UK, Republic of Ireland, Germany, New Zealand

scores.rationale: The 8-million-student global mobility market with low digital penetration is a credible secular pool, but the same calls show destination supply tightening in several corridors, which tempers the 'permanent expansion' claim.
scores.quote: If we talk about global student mobility, that number is 80 lakhs... the international education sector is structurally under-saturated with technology solutions

scores.rationale: Zero debt and 15 years of fully self-funded growth are strong stewardship evidence, offset by an explicit pivot to inorganic acceleration with four deals in one year and a stated intent to do more.
