scores.rationale: Management explicitly resists market pressure to accelerate e-commerce, choosing consolidation and model-fixing over land-grab, and holds the cluster strategy unchanged across all four calls.
scores.quote: some of you may think that, that should have been the year for speed or accelerated expansion of e-Commerce, we looked at it in a different way

scores.rationale: Single annual investor call, no forward guidance, understated tone throughout — Noronha describes a year of 41 store openings as routine.
scores.quote: So, it's a usual day at work, broadly, from that standpoint

scores.rationale: The apparel turnaround is credited explicitly to leadership pipeline building, though the CEO succession was filled externally (Anshul Asawa from Unilever) rather than internally, which cuts against a fully home-grown pipeline.
scores.quote: We just needed to build a very good leadership pipeline

scores.rationale: Management pre-empts uncomfortable questions and resets expectations downward rather than spinning — openly conceding GMA will not return to 27–28% and that apparel weakness was an internal failure.
scores.quote: we are not going to be 28% or 27% like it used to be earlier... it is more of an internal issue on the apparel side

scores.rationale: Reported metrics have softened on nearly every axis over the window (ROCE 19.1%→17.8%, EBITDA 8.7%→7.9%, LFL 9.9%→8.4%, e-commerce loss widening to INR247 crores), so the quality reputation is not currently being validated by improving results — the judgement rests on process discipline, not on a halo of outcomes.
scores.quote: the loss slightly widened to about 7%, the loss was at INR247 crores

scores.rationale: DMART owns the 'lowest price' position in the Indian value shopper's mind and drives traffic that no rival cluster matches, but this is a mental rather than structural monopoly and is being encroached on in apparel and quick commerce.
scores.quote: Another complement for our model is that because we drive so much of traffic

scores.rationale: Grocery retail has near-zero switching costs for the shopper — management's own commentary on customers moving to Myntra and Zudio for apparel confirms demand is contestable.
scores.quote: would you believe that online peers like Myntra or offline peers like Zudio are able to wean customers from our apparel offering?

scores.rationale: The end market is fragmenting rather than consolidating, with new value-apparel entrants at the sub-Rs 1,000 price point and quick-commerce players pressuring both offline and online channels.
scores.quote: the whole country has suddenly figured out that this is a space that has a huge opportunity. And you have a lot of players who are trying to get into this space

scores.rationale: DMART's owned-property, low-cost operating model is genuinely hard to replicate, but the window shows active new entry and price competition compressing gross margins rather than rational pricing.
scores.quote: in spite of the competitive context in the offline and the online space, our business has been resilient

scores.rationale: India's vast unorganised kirana trade and weak legacy modern-retail chains remain the structural donors of share to value formats, implied by the repeated framing of untapped headroom across population strata.
scores.quote: we see a tremendous headroom to grow both in the offline and the online channel

scores.rationale: The opposite holds — the category is the most crowded and capital-attracting space in Indian consumer, with everyone from Zudio to quick commerce piling in.
scores.quote: I think the whole country has suddenly figured out that this is a space that has a huge opportunity

scores.rationale: There is no image-based pricing power — the proposition is explicitly lowest price, gross margins slid 37 bps and EBITDA margin fell from 8.7% to 7.9% across the window.
scores.quote: Gross margin reduction of about 37 bps and PBT reduction of 43 bps led by the gross margin slide

scores.rationale: Customers trust DMART for consistent value and stock availability, but the calls give no evidence that price is secondary to trust — price is the entire proposition.

Cluster density and the Ready home-delivery pivot improve accessibility, but management concedes e-commerce convenience costs more to serve and that the market has moved toward delivery models DMART is still fixing.
scores.quote: we pivoted from the pickup, plus home delivery to a more focused home delivery business because that is how the market evolved

scores.rationale: The customer base is purely retail and the benefit offered — everyday low price — is correctly matched to that value-seeking shopper, delivering 35.3 crore bill cuts, though it is a price rather than intangible-based match.
scores.quote: We had about 35.3 crores bill cuts in the year just gone by

scores.rationale: No technology edge is claimed for the core business, and in the one tech-dependent arm management admits it is still work-in-progress with widening losses.
scores.quote: it's a conscious decision to fix the model, make it right and bring in high throughputs in the existing cities

scores.rationale: No two-sided network dynamic is described anywhere in the calls.

The cluster-based store and supply-chain density is the core structural advantage — it compounds operating leverage with each added store and is explicitly why capital is preferentially deployed in existing markets.
scores.quote: operating leverage gets better and better, if we have more and more stores opening in the same region

scores.rationale: Capex is unambiguously growth-oriented and rising (₹292cr in FY26 vs ₹210-225cr guided, ₹250-275cr planned for FY27, on a 45-acre greenfield plus brownfield and Jammu/Umargam land), but incremental returns look dilutive since EBITDA grew only 15.5% and PAT 12.2% against 21.6% revenue growth.
scores.quote: The company totally spent around INR292 crores in FY26 towards these objectives... we have lined up a capex plan between INR250 crores to INR275 crores for FY27.

scores.rationale: Sustained A&P — KBC sponsorship, events and digital — is visibly building brand equity (YouTube subscribers 3mn→4mn and Instagram to 170,000 across the year) alongside 21.6% revenue growth, though rising e-commerce A&M spend also compressed Q4 margin.
scores.quote: we also entered into a strategic partnership with Kaun Banega Crorepati as an official partner for the show

scores.rationale: No R&D spend or intensity is disclosed, but every quarter shows a consistent yield of new products (acrylic markers, mechanical pencils, metal pencil boxes, school bags, stamp pads) that management explicitly credits as a growth driver.
scores.quote: new product launches across categories with attractive ergonomic and user-friendly designs that resonated strongly with consumers and gained strong traction

scores.rationale: Deals are small and complementary (Super Treads for eastern paper stationery, a 50-50 JV with Seven SpA for premium bags), but the acquired Uniclan baby-hygiene business is explicitly margin-dilutive rather than OPM-accretive.
scores.quote: The EBITDA margin softened to 17.3% as compared to 18.2% in FY25 on account of higher Uniclan contribution in the overall consolidated operations.

scores.rationale: No buyback, dividend or distribution policy is discussed anywhere in the four calls; cash is being redirected entirely into capex.

This is an asset-heavy, backward-integrated manufacturer whose growth is explicitly gated by capacity additions, with ₹292cr of capex on ₹2,326cr of revenue and IPO proceeds consumed by fixed assets — the brand moat exists but the model is not asset-light.
scores.quote: Growth in certain categories, which were aided by capacity additions during the year, outpaced the growth in other categories.

scores.rationale: Long runway remains against a large unorganized segment, and GST 2.0 is explicitly cited as a catalyst shifting demand to branded players, with the Super Treads deal bought specifically to take paper-segment share in the East.
scores.quote: GST rate reduction on some of our core products creates a level playing field between organized and unorganized players, providing better market penetration opportunities and shift in demand towards branded products

scores.rationale: The FILA distribution tie-up has been converted into actual DOMS-branded exports to Chile, Mexico, Canada, Europe, Turkey, South Africa and Australia with 15%+ nine-month export growth despite US tariffs, though exports are now under 15% of sales and growing slower than domestic.
scores.quote: our distribution agreement with FILA has yielded positive results with initiation of exports of DOMS' branded stationery products to countries like Chile, Mexico, Canada, Europe, Turkey, South Africa and Australia

scores.rationale: Management repeatedly attributes growth predominantly to volume with only marginal ASP/mix contribution, and the FY27 pricing stance is explicitly subordinated to defending share.
scores.quote: This increase in sales was predominantly on account of volume growth aided by marginal increase in average selling prices due to change in product mix.

scores.rationale: The business is discussed as seasonal (back-to-school, winter diapers) and input-cost volatile rather than cyclical, and no cycle position or upturn is identified in any of the four calls.

The end market benefits from a genuine formalization and consumption tailwind — GST 2.0 rate cuts plus income tax reductions raising disposable income — but this is an India-penetration story rather than a globally expanding category.
scores.quote: these reforms, coupled with the income tax reductions introduced in budget 2025, will have a long-term positive impact by increasing the disposable income and uplifting consumer sentiment

scores.rationale: Growth is overwhelmingly organic and capacity-led with only small bolt-ons, funded from IPO proceeds and internal cash rather than leverage, and management committed to a larger FY27 capex precisely into a period of geopolitical uncertainty.
scores.quote: despite the current geopolitical and regulatory uncertainties, we have lined up a capex plan between INR250 crores to INR275 crores for FY27

scores.rationale: The multi-year 45-acre project has been pursued consistently through monsoon-driven delays with brownfield capacity deliberately bridging the gap, showing willingness to hold a long plan rather than abandon it.
scores.quote: This capacity expansion, along with other ongoing brownfield initiatives has been strategically planned and hence the delay should not materially impact our plans

scores.rationale: All four calls are run by the CFO alone with a matter-of-fact operational script and no promoter self-promotion, though the brand itself deliberately courts mass visibility via KBC and social media.
scores.quote: We have with us today senior management represented by Mr. Rahul Shah, Chief Financial Officer.

scores.rationale: Broad-based ESOP grants and explicit credit to employees indicate deliberate talent alignment, but there is no evidence of a systematic development programme or succession pipeline in these calls.
scores.quote: As a recognition of their ongoing contribution, we recently granted additional 137,690 ESOPs to the members of the DOMS family.

scores.rationale: Management quantified the GST transition drag, disclosed the 45-acre construction slippage twice and revised the timeline openly, and explained margin/PAT shortfalls by specific cause (Uniclan mix, lower other income from IPO cash deployment) rather than obscuring them.
scores.quote: we believe that if this transition impact would not be there, our sales could have been about 3% to 4% higher than what we reported for the quarter

scores.rationale: Results are strong and guidance was beaten, but a material part is attributable to tailwinds outside management skill (GST-led formalization, benign polymer/wax costs in Q3, capacity coming online) while margins and PAT growth actually decelerated — so the record does not cleanly isolate skill.
scores.quote: input costs for most goods had remained constant or were lower, especially for key raw materials like polymers, waxes, etc., providing a positive impact to our margins

scores.rationale: DOMS holds a strong mind-share position in stationery and art materials but the calls show it competing for penetration rather than occupying a monopoly-like slot, and there is no aftermarket or services annuity.
scores.quote: reinforcing DOMS as one of the most admired brands in stationery and art materials

scores.rationale: Consumer stationery carries essentially no switching costs and there is no captive aftermarket or regional exclusivity; management's own pricing caution implies customers can readily move.
scores.quote: any pricing action must be taken in a way that does not impact our market share or competitive positioning

scores.rationale: The market described is a mix of a few organized branded players and a large unorganized segment rather than a stable oligopoly, though the end customer is fragmented retail with no negotiating power.
scores.quote: GST rate reduction on some of our core products creates a level playing field between organized and unorganized players

scores.rationale: Pricing conduct is rational and gradual with no discount war mentioned and manufacturing scale is a real barrier, but the explicit subordination of price increases to share defence signals that pricing latitude is constrained rather than protected.
scores.quote: These include balanced and gradual approach to pricing and continued focus on cost efficiencies.

scores.rationale: A large unorganized cohort is the identified donator pool and the GST 2.0 rate cut is explicitly described as removing their cost advantage, creating a mechanical transfer of demand to branded players like DOMS.
scores.quote: providing better market penetration opportunities and shift in demand towards branded products

scores.rationale: Brand affinity is real and consumption margin held steady at 43.6% through raw-material volatility, but ASP increases are described as only marginal and pricing is constrained by share considerations, so image-based pricing power is moderate rather than strong.
scores.quote: Consumption margins were broadly consistent for FY26 at 43.6% similar to FY25.

scores.rationale: These are low-ticket consumer items bought on brand and availability rather than certainty of performance; no reliability-over-price dynamic appears in any of the four calls.

Management repeatedly credits an entrenched distribution network and channel partners as the growth engine, and bought Super Treads specifically to sit physically closer to eastern customers while scaling e-commerce reach.
scores.quote: strengthening our delivery capabilities in the Eastern region of the country... by getting us closer to our customers in that region

scores.rationale: The benefit mix matches the customer base — intangible brand pull and social-media affinity for the retail/student consumer, with a growing office-supplies line serving institutional buyers, though no switching-cost lock-in exists on the corporate side.
scores.quote: Quarterly growth was led by growth in categories across office supplies as we continue to see positive results on the back of enhanced capacities

scores.rationale: Advantage rests on manufacturing scale and design refresh, not technology; no R&D intensity, patents or technical differentiation is disclosed in any call.
scores.quote: The partnership combines FILA's global reach, presence, product designing and know-how and DOMS' manufacturing and execution capabilities.

scores.rationale: Nothing in the business model is two-sided or self-reinforcing — the 4 million YouTube subscribers are an audience, not a network that makes the product more valuable to other users.
scores.quote: YouTube subscribers have now crossed 4 million and Instagram followers are over 170,000

scores.rationale: Distribution is the clearest durable edge — an entrenched pan-India channel network cited as a primary growth driver, extended regionally via the Super Treads acquisition and globally by riding FILA's network into a dozen new countries.
scores.quote: the demand scenario in the domestic market continues to remain buoyant and was a key contributor to growth, underpinned by strong entrenched distribution network, robust brand equity

scores.rationale: Capex is modest and falling through the year (₹669cr Q3 → ₹438cr Q4 → ₹307cr Q1FY27, ₹2,302cr FY26) with ROCE ~20%, and the one clearly identifiable growth project — the semaglutide API scale-up — failed validation, so incremental returns are unproven.
scores.quote: Capex cash outflow for the quarter stood at ■307 crores, which is US$32 million

scores.rationale: SG&A is deliberately being raised 11–12% YoY as targeted brand investment behind NRT consumer healthcare and branded generics, but it has so far compressed margins without a visible branded-revenue payoff (NRT revenues declined).
scores.quote: ongoing, targeted investments to support long-term growth of our branded franchises, namely the acquired NRT consumer healthcare business and branded generics

scores.rationale: R&D is being cut (down 8–26% YoY, 7% of sales) with CAR-T discontinued and an in-licensed asset impaired, yet the same spend delivered first-to-market bosutinib, nintedanib, abatacept and first-ever Canadian semaglutide approval — productive but shrinking.
scores.quote: Impairment of ■135 crores... on account of discontinuation of R&D programs related to CAR-T therapy, as part of portfolio prioritisation

scores.rationale: BD has been bolt-on and complementary (NRT consumer healthcare, Immutep, Innoviva/XACDURO) but post-deal economics have worsened — NRT drove SG&A up while its revenue fell, and the Immutep in-licensed asset was impaired ₹93cr within months of signing after a futility analysis.
scores.quote: Impairment of ■93 crores on account of discontinuation of a trial by our partner, Immutep, of an in-licensed asset, Eftilagimod Alfa, following an interim futility analysis

scores.rationale: A routine ₹8/share dividend was declared out of a $349m net cash surplus, with no buyback and no articulated distribution policy discussed on any call.
scores.quote: the Board has recommended payment of a dividend of ■8 per equity share of face value Re. 1/- each

scores.rationale: The business is manufacturing-heavy with ₹14,353cr of operating working capital against ₹34,046cr of FY26 revenue (~0.4x on working capital alone), and the moat did not protect margins — gross margin fell ~500bps for the year.
scores.quote: Operating working capital as of 30th June 2026 was ■14,353 crores, which is US$1.52 billion

scores.rationale: The base business ex-lenalidomide compounded double-digit across all key geographies including North America on new launches, and in-licensed toripalimab crossed ₹100cr in under two years in India — genuine share capture, though headline revenue still declined.
scores.quote: the underlying base business, excluding lenalidomide, continued to deliver healthy double-digit growth across all key geographies, including North America

scores.rationale: Credible multi-market expansion in the window: first-to-approve-and-launch semaglutide in Canada, oral semaglutide in India, and an Innoviva partnership covering South/Central America, the Caribbean, Russia and CIS.
scores.quote: In Canada, we were the first company to secure approval for and launch semaglutide for the treatment of Type-2 diabetes

scores.rationale: Growth is driven by new launches, forex and branded mix while pricing is a persistent negative — price erosion in US and Europe generics is cited every quarter and dragged FY26 gross margin down 498bps.
scores.quote: The decline in margins was largely on account of lower lenalidomide sales and price erosion in our unbranded Generics businesses

scores.rationale: No cycle positioning is discussed; the lenalidomide decline is a product-exclusivity cliff rather than an end-market cycle, and the calls give no evidence of an identifiable industry upturn ahead.

The stated growth engines — peptides/GLP-1 metabolics, biosimilars and consumer health — sit in structurally expanding end markets, evidenced by the 6–7 million semaglutide pen commitment and the Nestlé nutrition tie-up.
scores.quote: building future growth engines in peptides, biosimilars, consumer health and innovation

scores.rationale: Net cash of $323–349m, no large acquisitions, an organic-first stance with only targeted BD, and active portfolio pruning (CAR-T exit, non-core India brand divestment for ₹189cr) indicate prudent stewardship.
scores.quote: targeted business development efforts to support our growth ambitions, while continuing to enhance efficiencies across operations

scores.rationale: The same two-pronged strategy is restated and executed consistently across all four calls, including a long-term supply arrangement with OneSource negotiated independent of the current setback.
scores.quote: We are entering into long-term arrangement with them, that we discussed unrelated to the current issue

scores.rationale: Management commentary is uniformly technical and substance-first — financial detail, validation timelines, batch-level facts — with no promotional or personality-driven framing anywhere in the four calls.
scores.quote: Patient safety and product quality remain our highest priorities and will continue to guide us in every decision we make

scores.rationale: The calls are silent on talent development or leadership pipeline; personnel is mentioned only as a cost line (annual increments, Labour Codes provision).

Exceptional candor: a dedicated call was convened within a day of learning of the semaglutide OOS result, each one-off was quantified separately, re-failure risk was volunteered, and an unrelated India recall was disclosed unprompted.
scores.quote: Is there a risk that we can fail again? Always. There is confidence, but naturally there is a risk of a further delay

scores.rationale: There is little halo risk to correct for — reported results are weak (Q1FY27 PAT ₹443cr, EBITDA margin 12.5%) and much of the swing is attributable to exogenous factors (lenalidomide cliff, forex, Middle East freight/solvent costs) rather than to demonstrated skill.
scores.quote: a decrease of 1,416 basis points YoY... reflecting a margin of 12.5% of the revenues

scores.rationale: Positions are time-boxed rather than monopoly-like — a 180-day bosutinib exclusivity that expires, and the lenalidomide franchise whose erosion is now the single largest drag on the P&L.
scores.quote: bosutinib, a first-to-market launch with a 180-day of generic drug exclusivity for the 400 mg strength

scores.rationale: Little evidence of switching-cost lock-in; the company itself is the substitutable party, and its own backup API source would take roughly a year to qualify, showing regulatory friction rather than customer captivity.
scores.quote: we do have a backup. It's not the same supplier. But this will require a pre-approval supplement... we are about one year away

scores.rationale: US and European unbranded generics show the opposite of a stable oligopoly — recurring price erosion and shelf stock adjustments (₹453cr on lenalidomide) demonstrate that customers hold the negotiating power.
scores.quote: A shelf stock adjustment or 'SSA' related to lenalidomide of ■453 crores, taken as a reduction in revenues

scores.rationale: Genuine technical barriers exist in peptides, biosimilars and complex generics (abatacept, semaglutide, nintedanib), but the unbranded generics base faces continuous discounting with no pricing rationality.
scores.quote: continued pricing pressure in US and Europe generics

scores.rationale: Competitors are never named or characterised in these calls, so there is no evidence of weak players from whom share is being taken.
The opposite of under-the-radar — triple-listed (NSE, BSE, NYSE), covered by HSBC and Bank of America on the calls, and able to convene an ad-hoc analyst call on one day's notice.
scores.quote: The first question is from the line of Damayanti Kerai from HSBC

scores.rationale: Gross margin fell to 46.5% in Q1FY27 (from ~57% a year earlier) under price erosion, indicating limited image- or taste-driven pricing power despite the India branded and NRT consumer franchises.
scores.quote: Consolidated gross profit margin was 46.5%, a decrease of 1,039 basis points YoY

scores.rationale: Reliability is the core promise and management defended it credibly (halting supply rather than shipping, no recall, cGMP compliance affirmed), but the episode itself was a failure to deliver certainty to a partner and market for several months.
scores.quote: if the process is not validated, we cannot send quantities to OneSource, and that's what created a halt of supply

scores.rationale: Reach exists via branded-generic field presence, NRT distributor networks and the Nestlé nutrition tie-up, but nothing in the calls demonstrates superior accessibility or customer intimacy versus peers.
scores.quote: complemented by nutrition offerings such as Celevida 'GLP +' through our collaboration with Nestlé

scores.rationale: The portfolio straddles both types — retail-facing branded/consumer in India and Emerging Markets, corporate-facing unbranded generics in US/Europe — but the corporate side shows no lock-in and the retail side no evident premium capture.
scores.quote: Strong performance across our Branded businesses, namely India, Emerging Markets and the acquired consumer healthcare business in Nicotine Replacement Therapy (NRT)

scores.rationale: Real multi-product complex capability — synthetic peptide semaglutide API, abatacept biosimilar, first-to-market bosutinib and nintedanib — at 7% of sales R&D, though the API scale-up failure and falling R&D temper the edge.
scores.quote: we scaled up the synthetic API manufacturing process at our API facility, with the intent of increasing the API output

scores.rationale: No network effect exists or is claimed — the model is manufacture-and-supply through partners and distributors, where scale brings cost, not self-reinforcing demand.

Broad multi-geography commercial reach is the asset in-licensors buy — Immutep, Innoviva and toripalimab were all placed with Dr. Reddy's for markets spanning India, Emerging Markets, LatAm, the Caribbean and Russia/CIS.
scores.quote: we partnered with Innoviva Specialty Therapeutics to develop and commercialise, XACDURO®... in select markets across South and Central America, the Caribbean, Russia and CIS countries

scores.rationale: Management points to physical runway for expansion (30 acres at Bangalore, 90 acres at Sulur) and ramping A220 door production, but gives no capex figures or incremental ROIC evidence, and historically avoided buying machines in India.
scores.quote: we have unique access to this runway for our future production. We have a similar 90 Acres

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend in the window.

Self-developed adjacent hydraulic products (power lift, bar steering) now in customer testing plus an IP-rich UK pump product show R&D converting into new products, though no R&D spend or efficiency data is given.
scores.quote: these are products that we've developed... We have just started testing this with customers

scores.rationale: M&A described is a small complementary bolt-on (buying its UK pump competitor in Swindon) alongside divestment of commoditised automotive units, but no post-deal margin evidence is offered.
scores.quote: we have a large plant where we bought our competitor in Swindon, UK

scores.rationale: Only debt reduction from the wind-farm monetisation is mentioned; no buyback, dividend or distribution policy is discussed.
scores.quote: we just used it to pay down debt

scores.rationale: The moat is real (sole-source Airbus work, one-in-three tractor pumps) but the business is asset-heavy — German foundry, UK robotic machining, multiple plants and large land banks — and no turnover metrics are disclosed.
scores.quote: We still own one of the world's best automotive foundries, which is in Germany

scores.rationale: Gear-pump share is already very large (limited runway), but aerospace offers real capture — the A220 full door-suite order is described as the largest such order in India — plus a market-share-to-wallet-share push in hydraulics.
scores.quote: this is going from market share to wallet share

scores.rationale: Genuinely globalised and well-executed footprint (Bangalore, Swindon UK, Germany, small North America) serving Airbus and Boeing, though this is an established structure rather than fresh expansion.
scores.quote: We have significant manufacturing in uh Germany in UK and a very small facility in North America

scores.rationale: Growth story is explicitly content/mix escalation — single pump to double pump to power-lift systems, and £2,000 UK pumps — although regulation-driven pump volume is also cited and no realised revenue split is given.
scores.quote: that 1,800-rupee pump becomes some 4,500-rupee double pump... there's a 25/30,000 rupee power lift system

scores.rationale: Company cites a Q2 pause in the UK pump business that has since bounced back, and sits early in a post-pandemic commercial aerospace ramp with a defence hedge.
scores.quote: the second quarter we had taken a pause. We talked about and it sort of bounced back

scores.rationale: End markets are in long secular expansion — global aerostructures ramp on A320/A220, Indian defence indigenisation (Tejas, F-15EX), and a multi-decade infrastructure/urbanisation cycle for hydraulics.
scores.quote: this entire infra boom that we're going to see for the next 25/30 years

scores.rationale: Evidence of discipline — exiting commoditised automotive machining and foundries, monetising the wind farm to repay debt, and refusing to buy expensive machines where economics did not work — offset by no leverage numbers being disclosed.
scores.quote: which we sold because it became a commodity

scores.rationale: Founder-CEO has run a single long-term thesis for four decades, from a distressed 1.5-crore pump shop to sole-source Airbus aerostructures, including an explicit 8-10 year rebuild of the business mix.
scores.quote: over the last 8/10 years we spent just rejigging what was a typical automotive business

scores.rationale: The interaction is a high-profile showcase built around the founder's personal story and a ministerial launch event, the opposite of low-profile, substance-over-celebrity communication.
scores.quote: Seated with us uh in this very important occasion, uh Minister of State, General Dr VK Singh Saab

scores.rationale: Deep internal pipeline is demonstrated in detail — CFO promoted from financial controller, 26-year COO, a worker now GM of a subsidiary, a stenographer turned star salesman, and second-generation employees.
scores.quote: we grew people from inside because the company was in a great distress

scores.rationale: The presentation is almost entirely narrative and capability showcase with essentially no financial disclosure, guidance, or acknowledgement of shortfalls beyond a passing reference to a quarter's pause.
scores.quote: this capability, is on the left side of the P &L account, it's all on the cost side

scores.rationale: The assessment is highly exposed to halo — marquee logos (Airbus, Boeing, DRDO), an awards-and-ministers framing and a founder legend, with no margin, ROCE or cash-flow evidence to separate results from skill.
scores.quote: One company out of 18,000 wins this

scores.rationale: Genuine monopoly-like positions: sole supplier of the flap track beam assembly across the entire A320 family and roughly a third of all tractors built globally carrying its pump.
scores.quote: we became the sole supplier for the flap track beam assembly for the A318, A319, A320,and A321

scores.rationale: Aerospace qualification, single-sourcing and liability-backed supply agreements create heavy switching costs, and the customer/supplier financing arrangement is described as a lock-in, though no aftermarket annuity is evidenced.
scores.quote: A customer and our supplier help us in a financial, it's a complete lock in

scores.rationale: Supply may be concentrated, but the end customers are Airbus, Boeing and large tractor OEMs who hold overwhelming negotiating power, including day-rate liability terms imposed on the supplier.
scores.quote: you've signed agreements of liability with these customers, and every day is gonna cost you a million dollars

scores.rationale: Barriers are clearly high — India's largest corporates were rejected for lacking aerospace knowledge, qualified raw material remains unavailable domestically — but nothing is said about pricing discipline among incumbents.
scores.quote: the raw material was not available in India, even today is not available in India

scores.rationale: Weak competitors are evident: pandemic bankruptcies among commercial jetliner suppliers, and the prior producer of the flap track beam whose looser tolerances required shimming.
scores.quote: lot of suppliers to uh commercial jet liners across the world went bankrupt

scores.rationale: The complex aerostructures niche is one large Indian conglomerates could not enter, but the company itself is now anything but under the radar, launching record orders at national ministerial events.
scores.quote: They went to all the big companies, all the top three names that you can think of... none of them had aerospace knowledge

scores.rationale: No discussion of image- or taste-driven pricing power or gross margin; the customer base is industrial OEMs where this benefit type does not apply and no margin data is given.

Customers buy safety-critical certainty — pressurised doors cycling 30-40,000 times without leaking, tolerance improvements that removed shimming, best-supplier status on Sukhoi and Airbus's first sustainability award.
scores.quote: it has to open and close 30,000 times 40,000 times in its life without leaking, under pressure

scores.rationale: Dispersed engineering placed close to customers (Bangalore, France, Swindon, German material science) plus a UK plant near Heathrow gives real customer intimacy, though sales-force reach is only described historically.
scores.quote: dispersed engineering capability of a Bangalore based company with engineers in Bangalore, in France, in Swindon

scores.rationale: Customer set is entirely corporate (Airbus, Boeing, DRDO, tractor OEMs) and the benefits offered — reliability, cost-optimised global supply chain and qualification lock-in — are correctly matched to that type.
scores.quote: we take advantage of the low cost of labour here low cost of capital there

scores.rationale: Credible multi-product engineering edge — 5-10 micron pump tolerances transferred into aerostructures, destructive test labs, material science, IP-rich hydraulic products — but no R&D intensity figures are provided.
scores.quote: we were used to in hydraulic pumps 5-micron 10 micron, here you had 50 Micron

scores.rationale: No two-sided network or self-reinforcing scale dynamic is described anywhere in the window.
Only the founder's 1980s mechanic-introduction sales approach is described; no current distribution or service-reach advantage is discussed.

Capex is clearly growth-directed — new delivery centres (Lima, Cairo) plus ~1,550 new seats across Airoli, Pune and Chandigarh during FY26 — and it coincided with 18% USD revenue growth and 132bps of full-year margin expansion, implying good incremental returns on an asset-light base.
scores.quote: On the new centers, we have recently opened our Lima operations, which went live this quarter, and operations in Cairo will be going live in Q2.

scores.rationale: A&P appears only as higher travel/marketing and S&D variable payouts in Q3 with no evidence of durable brand-equity building, though S&D spend does track improving win rates and deal sizes.
scores.quote: Increase in sales and distribution variable payouts and higher travel and marketing costs are the major contributers to the Q-o-Q margin decline.

scores.rationale: Product investment is visibly converting into revenue — Market360, Compliance Manager and the Roboworx CogniFlows agentic platform, a first large-scale Agentic AI win in Q4, and Analytics & Automation reaching a $90m book — although R&D spend itself is never quantified.
scores.quote: Analytics and automation is now a USD 90 million book. That is a significant milestone, and this area will continue to attract focused investment

scores.rationale: No new M&A in the window and the one legacy bolt-on referenced (Personiv) is performing, with the F&A-led emerging business growing strongly for three consecutive quarters.
scores.quote: The Personiv brand continues to carry strong recall among SMBs seeking F&A automation.

scores.rationale: A coherent package was executed — INR 300cr buyback completed with 625,000 shares extinguished, promoters abstaining, plus a 1:1 bonus and INR 1 dividend — but the buyback was priced at INR 4,500 versus a market price near INR 4,400 after a strong run, i.e. not at a depressed valuation.
scores.quote: what made you come up with the share price of INR 4,500 when the date on which you declared your results, the closing share price was closer to INR 4,400

scores.rationale: Asset-light services model: FY26 generated INR 8,729mn operating cash and INR 7,560mn FCF (implying ~INR 1.2bn capex on INR 42.2bn revenue) with the best OCF/EBITDA conversion in five years, though the protecting moat is only moderate.
scores.quote: the OCF-to-EBITDA ratio is 75%, the highest in the last 5 years.

scores.rationale: Clear share capture from a small base against a weak macro — 18% USD growth, top-10 concentration falling from 63-64% to 59%, non-top-10 outgrowing top-10 every quarter, and a rising count of $1m/$3m/$5m clients.
scores.quote: Top 10 client concentration has come down to 59% from 63% to 64%, a healthy sign of portfolio diversification

scores.rationale: Delivery-footprint expansion is credible and well-executed — Lima and Cairo went live within the year, Cairo hit top-quartile performance four months into production and already has multiple clients signed, with Manila and Fayetteville next.
scores.quote: It showed up top quartile performance just four months into production... we are seeing preliminary interest from other clients for Cairo as a location.

scores.rationale: Growth is substantially volume/headcount-led (bottom-of-pyramid hiring, seat additions, higher headcount pressuring Q4 margin) with no pricing power cited; the offsetting positive is genuine mix improvement toward higher-value Analytics & Automation and longer-term deals.
scores.quote: thanks to the strong top line growth in BFSI and CMT Offshore, enabling us to hire at the bottom of the pyramid.

scores.rationale: The Fashion & Luxury vertical appears to be at or near a cyclical trough with an identifiable upturn management expects in H1 FY27, giving a recovery kicker to an otherwise flat segment.
scores.quote: our CLX business is expected to return to growth in H1 FY '27, supported by new GenAI wins at a key client, as well as what we are seeing as some positive green shoots

scores.rationale: End markets — KYC/financial-crime compliance, digital operations and now agentic AI deployment — show durable secular demand, though the same AI wave is a two-sided risk to an FTE-linked delivery model.
scores.quote: long-term demand for our services remains firmly intact, and our pipeline is strong

scores.rationale: Purely organic growth with no acquisitions, a healthy balance sheet, capacity investment sustained through a weak macro, and cash returned via buyback and dividend rather than deployed into large deals.
scores.quote: We enter FY '27 with conviction. Our balance sheet is healthy.

scores.rationale: Management points to a strategy set ~10-11 quarters earlier now visibly compounding, and analysts corroborate seven consecutive quarters of steady delivery against those plans.
scores.quote: whatever we have seen is in line with what we had laid out about 10, 11 quarters back in terms of the strategy. And I think we are beginning to see the benefits

scores.rationale: Calls are plain and metric-driven, with credit deflected to clients and employees and no headline guidance or self-promotion, even in a record year.
scores.quote: None of this happens without the trust our clients place in us, the commitment our people bring every day

scores.rationale: Systematic, large-scale capability building — 8,000 employees (40% of headcount) upskilled on GenAI with TU Munich, 3,000+ trained on agentic AI and vibe coding, firm-wide Copilot rollout, GPTW certification and a third consecutive talent-development award — alongside attrition below historical levels.
scores.quote: 8,000 employees have successfully upskilled, which represents roughly 40% of our employee count.

scores.rationale: Consistently candid: unpacked the weak Q1 cash flow into DSO, gratuity and bonus drivers, attributed most of Q2's margin beat to FX and pre-warned Q3 and Q4 softness, disclosed the offshore-call NPRM risk, and switched to the operating-EBITDA metric investors asked for.
scores.quote: We expect that Q3 margins will not be as strong as Q2, given that the INR has appreciated recently.

scores.rationale: Headline results are flattered by factors outside management skill — 200 of the 270bps Q2 margin expansion came from FX and growth leans on headcount addition — so the record year should not be read as pure execution alpha, even though client diversification and new-centre ramps are genuine skill signals.
scores.quote: the margin expansion has been about 270 bps, 200 bps of which came from FX

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like hold on the customer: roughly 15-20% of the top line rolls off every year, indicating work is recompeted rather than owned.
scores.quote: Yes, about the same, there is no significant change in roll-off percentages.

scores.rationale: Some switching-cost stickiness exists — tenured relationships, an AI-native KYC orchestrator embedded across multiple client systems, and steady upsell/cross-sell — but it is offset by persistent double-digit roll-offs and no captive aftermarket.
scores.quote: Our AI-native orchestrator for KYC case management is live across multiple client systems.

scores.rationale: eClerx competes in a fragmented outsourcing market against far larger vendors, and clients retain clear negotiating leverage given their standing cost focus.
scores.quote: Clients continue to remain focused on cost control and operational efficiencies.

scores.rationale: Barriers are low in an outsourcing market where buyers press for cost reduction and pricing is competitively bid; domain specialisation and Everest/Gartner placements provide only partial protection.
scores.quote: client spend is concentrated on transformation and customer experience programs to reduce cost

scores.rationale: Wins are described as a mix of new-logo acquisition and cross-sell without identifying weak competitors being displaced, so share gain is evident but the donator dynamic is not established.
scores.quote: it's a combination of both, new customer acquisitions as well as cross-sell and upsell

scores.rationale: The company operates in unglamorous specialist niches — capital-markets operations, digital shelf analytics, KYC case management — where its recognitions come in narrow category matrices rather than mainstream attention.
scores.quote: we were named a representative vendor in the Gartner Market Guide for Digital Shelf Analytics for our Market360 solution

scores.rationale: Margins are healthy (25-28% EBITDA) but the value proposition is explicitly cost and efficiency rather than image or taste, and demand in Fashion & Luxury proved far from steady through the year.
scores.quote: Fashion and Luxury had a sluggish year

scores.rationale: Clients buy reliability — expansion is repeatedly credited to delivery quality and trust rather than price, with Everest buyers citing transparency and proactive relationship management and existing clients following eClerx into a brand-new Cairo centre.
scores.quote: We are continuing to upsell and cross-sell on the back of strong delivery, commitment to innovation and insights and strategic relationships.

scores.rationale: A widening multi-geography delivery grid (Lima, Cairo, Manila, Fayetteville) plus onshore consulting and new inbound sales capability give clients accessibility and time-zone coverage close to their operations.
scores.quote: geographic diversification conversations are gaining real traction, with client expansions exploring into Manila, Cairo and Fayetteville.

scores.rationale: Customers are corporates and the pitch is correctly matched to them — TCO, automation, compliance certainty and embedded systems work — rather than intangible brand appeal.
scores.quote: conversations around KYC, financial crime compliance, and AI-led transformation are progressing well.

scores.rationale: A real multi-product tech stack is emerging — Roboworx CogniFlows, Market360, Compliance Manager, an agentic data-sourcing platform — validated by Everest/Gartner placements and a first large-scale agentic AI win, but it is not yet a deep, defensible edge versus larger vendors.
scores.quote: our rapid advancements in Agentic AI driven by Roboworx CogniFlows, our enterprise-grade Agentic Automation platform.

scores.rationale: The calls contain no evidence of any two-sided or self-reinforcing network dynamic in the business model.

A multi-continent delivery and service network (India, Egypt, Peru, Philippines, US) with 90+ clients above $0.5m and expanding sales capability gives useful reach where service execution is decisive, though rivals of scale can match it.
scores.quote: 90 clients now contribute $0.5 million or more in revenue.
