scores.quote: On NCR, I am pleased to share that our operations they are now EBITDA positive on a full year basis

scores.rationale: Mix is improving toward premium (larger TVs, dishwashers, front-load washers lifting ASP), but headline growth is store-count and GST-cut volume driven and gross margin fell because of extra discounting.
scores.quote: the decline in gross margin is majorly due to extra discounts we provided in the quarter

scores.rationale: The year began at a cyclical trough (coolest summer in years, LTL -18%) and ended with clear upturn signals — GST cuts, rate cuts and income-tax relief driving Q4 revenue +15% and SSSG +12.2%.
scores.quote: Interest rates have been reduced, GST rates have come down and the government has also reduced income tax slabs previously

scores.rationale: End market is structurally expanding through low category penetration and premiumisation, with new categories like dishwashers and induction cooktops gaining traction.
scores.quote: Several categories in our portfolio continue to remain unpenetrated, offering significant growth potential

scores.rationale: Focus is organic with no big M&A and a non-core divestment, but the aggressive store roll-out has pushed up finance costs and depreciation and depressed PAT and ROCE, so prudence is questionable.
scores.quote: The rapid expansion has also led to higher financing costs and depreciation due to the IndAS 116 lease accounting impact

scores.rationale: Promoter-CEO has persisted with the multi-year NCR build-out through years of losses until it turned EBITDA positive, and continues investing through a weak demand year.
scores.quote: We expect many of these stores to mature over the next couple of years and start delivering better margins

scores.rationale: Calls are run by just the promoter-CEO and CFO in a plain, operational register with no self-promotion or celebrity framing.
scores.quote: Along with me, I have Mr. Premchand Devarakonda, our Chief Financial Officer

scores.rationale: Talent development and leadership pipeline are never discussed; manpower appears only as a cost line.

Disclosure is unusually granular and self-critical — they split mature vs new store revenue and margins, disclosed the fire loss and accounting reclassification, reported negative LTL of 18%, and admitted margin loss came from their own discounting.
scores.quote: Like-to-like sales growth for the quarter was negative 18%

scores.rationale: Management attributes the strong Q4 SSSG to external tailwinds (GST cut, big mobile launches) rather than claiming skill, making it easy to separate results from execution.
scores.quote: I would attribute this majority of the sales coming in from a lot of benefit that has come our way, especially post-September the benefit of GST dropped

scores.rationale: Bajaj Electronics has a strong decades-old position in the Hyderabad customer's mind but is not monopoly-like, as new players are actively entering its core markets.
scores.quote: despite the entry of new players into these markets, we have been able to sustain our market share

scores.rationale: Durables retail carries essentially zero switching costs and no captive aftermarket; regional density in Telangana/AP is being contested by new entrants and online channels.
scores.quote: despite the entry of new players into these markets

scores.rationale: The market is fragmented and contested with the end customer holding full negotiating power — management had to push sales with extra discounts during the GST-transition slowdown.
scores.quote: we have to just push some sales by offering additional discounts that has marginally reduced the margins

scores.rationale: Low barriers are evident from fresh competitor entry into the core southern markets combined with discount-led sales pushes.
scores.quote: despite the entry of new players into these markets, we have been able to sustain our market share

scores.rationale: Growth is coming from organised-retail penetration in under-served up-country and NCR markets, where weaker unorganised/regional retailers cede share as EMIL adds stores.
scores.quote: our NCR cluster continued to scale up well, achieving a revenue growth of 38% and an SSG of 11%

scores.rationale: The company is low-profile and regionally focused, but its markets are visibly attracting competitive capital, so it is not an ignored niche.
scores.quote: despite the entry of new players into these markets

scores.rationale: Margins are thin and price-driven — EBITDA margin of only 6.1% for FY26 and gross margin sacrificed to discounting — indicating little image-based pricing power.
scores.quote: EBITDA margin for FY26 stood at 6.1%

scores.rationale: Management positions customer experience and a decades-old service reputation as the core proposition, and mature stores sustain ~7.3% margins on that basis.
scores.quote: we will continue to invest in customer experience, because that is what we have defined EMIL's reputation over decades

scores.rationale: Dense cluster-based store network (223 stores) with deliberate deepening of existing clusters and strong on-ground execution gives superior local accessibility.
scores.quote: We will deepen our presence in existing clusters while remaining selective about new geographies

scores.rationale: Customers are retail consumers, but the offer is matched mainly on convenience and service rather than a strong intangible/brand pull, with discounting still needed to move stock.
scores.quote: customers are increasingly opting for large televisions and higher-priced air conditioners

scores.rationale: No proprietary technology or R&D intensity is discussed; technology appears only as products sold (AI-enabled devices).
No two-sided network dynamic is described anywhere in the calls.
The 223-store clustered network with supply-chain and inventory calibration is the main durable advantage, evidenced by well-managed AC inventory into the summer season.
scores.quote: maintaining a well-calibrated mix of carry forward and of new AC models ensuring we were well positioned heading into the summer season

scores.rationale: Large, funded growth capex — a 6 GW integrated TOPCon cell+module plant at ~INR 5,500 crores taking capacity to 16.3 GW modules / 8.9 GW cells — on top of two 2.5 GW module lines already commissioned, with FY26 ROCE of 38% and ROE of 51% evidencing high incremental returns.
scores.quote: The total project cost is estimated at approximately INR 5,500 crores... our total manufacturing capacity is expected to increase to approximately 16.3 gigawatt of modules and 8.9 gigawatt of cells

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend in any of the four calls.

Process R&D staffed with PhDs has delivered a measurable result — silver paste consumption per cell halved since the line started, with a further 40% reduction targeted — plus early TOPCon adoption and G12R launch, but management could not quantify R&D spend when asked.
scores.quote: Because of improved technology, design and process R&D the consumption of silver paste has come down drastically and the targeted consumption of silver paste, there is an opportunity to bring it down another 40%

scores.rationale: No acquisitions were made or discussed in the window; the only purchase mentioned is land for the Devanahalli greenfield project.
No dividend, buyback or distribution policy was discussed; IPO proceeds were applied to debt prepayment rather than shareholder returns.

Deeply asset-heavy model — INR 5,049 crores of FY26 revenue against a capacity base absorbing another INR 5,500 crores of capex, with module utilization stuck at 43-45%, so asset turn is structurally low even though ROCE is currently high on policy-driven margins.
scores.quote: Effective module capacity utilization stood at 45% compared to 44% in both Q1 FY26 and Q4 FY26

scores.rationale: Order book grew from ~5 GW to 9.9 GW across the four calls and FY26 revenue rose 116% with module production doubling and cell production tripling — clear share capture from a small base with ample runway.
scores.quote: our order book increased to 9.9 gigawatt of the end of the quarter compared to 9.4 gigawatt at the end of FY2026

scores.rationale: Exports are named as a strategic intent but no executed geographic expansion, export revenue or overseas customer wins are disclosed in any call.
scores.quote: strengthening relationships with IPPs, Utilities, EPCs, Corporates, and international customers with focus on export as part of our strategic roadmap

scores.rationale: Growth is overwhelmingly volume-led (module production 1,482 MW to 2,999 MW; cells 534 MW to 1,520 MW) in a market where unit prices fall structurally and raw-material moves are contractually passed through, with mix (cell integration) a secondary contributor.
scores.quote: when we started the manufacturing in 2006 of modules the price of module was €3 per watt but today the price is 15 cents

scores.rationale: Positioned ahead of an identifiable upturn — ALMM List 2 from June 2026 expands the DCR market as grandfathered non-DCR projects roll off, while domestic high-efficiency TOPCon cell supply remains tight.
scores.quote: Domestic supply of high-efficiency TOPCon cells continues to remain relatively tight, which should support the operating environment for established and compliant cell manufacturers

scores.rationale: End market is in genuine secular expansion — rising electricity demand, energy security, EVs, storage, green hydrogen and data centres, reinforced by PM Surya Ghar, PM-KUSUM and the ALMM localisation ladder.
scores.quote: Growing electricity demand, increasing energy security, domestic manufacturing initiative, electric mobility, energy storage, green hydrogen, and data centers are creating a significant long-term opportunity

scores.rationale: Purely organic expansion with conspicuous balance-sheet prudence — INR 1,621 crores of term loans prepaid from IPO proceeds, net debt/equity at negative 0.06x, current ratio 2.1x, expansion debt tied up at sub-8%, and rating upgraded twice from BBB- to A.
scores.quote: As of March 31, 2026, our net debt to equity stood at negative 0.06x. Our current ratio improved to 2.1x.

scores.rationale: Founder-led over three decades from solar water heaters to integrated PV, an early mover into TOPCon cells, now sequencing further backward integration into ingot and wafer — long-term intent visible, though only one year of listed delivery is available to verify it.
scores.quote: we have grown from small solar water heater manufacturing into one of the leading Indian integrated solar manufacturing companies

scores.rationale: A closely held Bengaluru family business for thirty years that only began speaking publicly after its November 2025 listing, with no celebrity positioning, though the chairman's scripted remarks lean on aspirational language.
scores.quote: Over the last few months, we have experienced a remarkable transition from a closely held organization to a publicly listed enterprise

scores.rationale: Beyond a PhD-staffed process R&D team and generic thanks to employees, there is no evidence of systematic talent development or an internal leadership pipeline; the CEO role sits with the founder's family.
scores.quote: Emmvee has a team of process R&D, who hold PhDs, and they are focused on process improvements

scores.rationale: Management volunteered unflattering detail (module utilization of only 43%) and pushed back on an analyst's flattering percentage-margin framing to insist on absolute EBITDA per watt, though it deflected an R&D-spend question for lack of numbers.
scores.quote: Don't look at percentage of margin... that should not simply give you a wrong perspective if it inflates the percentage

scores.rationale: Spectacular headline results (116% revenue growth, 51% ROE, 35% EBITDA margin) rest heavily on ALMM/DCR protection, a first full year of cell operations and post-IPO deleveraging rather than demonstrated durable skill, so the outcomes flatter the assessment.
scores.quote: ALMM 1 created the foundation for approved module manufacturing. The next phase is more important for integrated manufacturers.

scores.rationale: Modules and cells are sold as spec-driven commodities to IPPs, EPCs and utilities with pass-through raw-material contracts and no aftermarket or services annuity — nothing resembling a monopoly in the customer's mind.
scores.quote: our contracts are most of them backed by pass through contracts so any major changes in materials are passed on to the customer

scores.rationale: ALMM List 2 confers a regulatory ring-fence around domestic cell supply that functions like a partial monopoly today, but it is shared with every listed peer and creates no customer switching costs.
scores.quote: Our operational TOPCon cell manufacturing facility and inclusion under ALMM List 2 position us well

scores.rationale: Compliant domestic TOPCon cell supply is currently tight and concentrated, but the customer base is large utilities and IPPs with real negotiating power and management itself expects the field to widen.
scores.quote: Competition will increase, technology will evolve, trade rules will change

scores.rationale: Capital is the only real barrier in a sector where module ASPs have collapsed from €3/W to 15 cents/W and management explicitly warns of rising competition and volatile commodity cycles — historically an industry of discount wars, not rational pricing.
scores.quote: the environment is also more complex. Competition will increase, technology will evolve, trade rules will change, logistic and commodity cycles may remain volatile

scores.rationale: ALMM List 2 forcibly disqualifies imported (largely Chinese) cells from covered projects, creating a pool of displaced volume that compliant domestic manufacturers can absorb as grandfathered non-DCR projects complete.
scores.quote: We expect DCR demand to strengthen progressively during FY2027 as grandfathered non-DCR projects are completed

scores.rationale: The opposite of obscure — a November 2025 IPO raising INR 2,900 crores into India's most capital-attracting manufacturing theme, with analyst-covered quarterly calls and a sector drawing large-scale competing investment.
scores.quote: We completed our IPO and public listing in November 2025, raising INR2,900 crores

scores.rationale: Gross margin of 47% and EBITDA margin of 35-36% are genuinely high, but they derive from DCR/ALMM protection, integration and tight cell supply rather than any brand or image-based pricing power in a spec-bought product.
scores.quote: Gross profit was 543.8 crores with a gross margin of about 47%

scores.rationale: Modules are a 25-year bankability decision and management consistently anchors the pitch on quality, reliability and traceability backed by a three-decade record and ALMM listing, which matters more to project financiers than headline price.
scores.quote: it will belong to companies that can participate deeper in the value chain, maintain quality, improve traceability and reduce dependence on external supply chains

scores.rationale: No discussion of distribution reach, channel structure or sales-force intimacy in any of the four calls.

The customer base is correctly corporate (utility-scale, C&I and rooftop developers) and the 4.5 GW multi-year TOPCon cell order shows some lock-in, but pass-through pricing and commodity specification mean no durable switching-cost advantage is demonstrated.
scores.quote: our order book was about 9.3 GW including the 4.5 GW multi-year Topcon cell order

scores.rationale: Early TOPCon adoption, 100% TOPCon module capacity and G12R launch show competence, but the technology is equipment-vendor supplied and industry-standard, with the edge confined to process yield rather than a proprietary multi-product platform.
scores.quote: Our aggregate module capacity now reflects a 100% transition to TOPCon technology

scores.rationale: A single-sided B2B manufacturing model selling modules and cells to project developers — nothing in the calls describes any self-reinforcing network, and none exists structurally.
The 9.9 GW order book spans utility, C&I and rooftop channels, but no service network, dealer reach or delivery capability that rivals cannot replicate is described.
scores.quote: reflects continued demand across utility-scale, commercial and industrial, and rooftop solar segments

scores.rationale: Four simultaneous greenfield growth projects (AURIC Shendra castings, Bidkin alloy wheels, Chennai brakes, battery packs) plus a 5x ABS capacity expansion, with capacity pre-booked by OEM orders rather than maintenance spend.
scores.quote: All the above four Greenfield plants, will be fully operational over the next few quarters, and we will feel the full impact in the second half of FY 27.

scores.rationale: No advertising or promotion spend is discussed in any of the four calls; as a B2B OEM component supplier the topic never arises.

Two new R&D centres commissioned within the window (suspension R&D at Waluj operational July 2025, integrated brakes/ABS R&D double the prior size commissioned January 2026) and R&D is visibly converting into new products and customers — dual-channel ABS, in-house ECUs, BMS across 2W/3W/tractors.
scores.quote: Our new integrated R&D facility for brakes was commissioned in January 2026 at Waluj... This facility is double the size of the existing one and integrates two-wheeler brakes and ABS R&D

scores.rationale: Two small complementary bolt-ons — Stöferle in Europe and buying the residual 38.5% of Maxwell to reach 100% — with Maxwell already performing (H1 FY26 revenue exceeded all of FY25), though post-deal margin impact is not disclosed.
scores.quote: In Q1 of FY 26, we accelerated the purchase of the balance 38.5% stake in Maxwell. We are now 100% owners of this business

scores.rationale: No dividend, buyback or distribution policy is mentioned in any of the four calls.

The business is structurally asset-heavy — die casting presses of 1,100T–2,500T, alloy wheel plants, brake machining lines — and is currently adding four greenfield plants, which depresses asset turns further before revenue ramps.
scores.quote: Die casting press machines ranging from 1,100T to 2,500T are planned to align with market trends towards higher tonnage and light weighting

scores.rationale: Standalone growth consistently outran the industry (10.1% in Q1 FY26 against 2W volumes down 1.6%; 16.2% against 10.3%) and new content wins keep landing at OEMs where it was previously absent — TVS and Hero inverted forks, Tata 4W drum brakes, JLR and a large US EV OEM at Shendra.
scores.quote: 2W sales reached 5.81 million units in Q1 FY26, down 1.6% year-on-year... Endurance in its standalone financials for Q1 FY26 saw a year-on-year growth of 10.1%.

scores.rationale: Genuine expansion on two fronts — South India via Chennai/Vallam plants sited next to TVS, Royal Enfield, Yamaha, Hyundai, Kia and Isuzu, and exports to US/UK OEMs — but European organic growth is thin (0.6% and 7.8% ex-Stöferle) in a challenging market.
scores.quote: If we also remove the impact of the Stöferle acquisition, our top line in Europe grew by 0.6%.

scores.rationale: Mix is genuinely improving toward higher value-add (ABS, in-house ECUs, BMS, battery packs), but the headline growth is volume- and new-order-driven, and pricing is a cost pass-through negotiation with OEMs rather than a source of power.
scores.quote: regular interactions with customers to update them on input cost increases, including gas and oil

scores.rationale: The Indian 2W cycle is already well into an upturn rather than near its bottom — volumes accelerated from -1.6% in Q1 FY26 to +25.4% in Q4 FY26 on the GST cut — so the cyclical entry point is late, while Europe remains soft.
scores.quote: 2W sales reached 7.2 million units in Q4 of FY 26, up 25.4% year-on-year, with motorcycles at 19.8% growth and scooters at 37.1% growth.

scores.rationale: The ABS mandate is a regulated five-fold step-up in addressable market that also pulls through disc brakes, layered on EV content growth (BMS, battery packs, motor housings) — permanent content-per-vehicle expansion, not cyclical volume.
scores.quote: The new safety requirements are expected to increase the ABS requirement in India 5-fold. Higher ABS use would also lead to higher disc brake penetration.

scores.rationale: Growth is overwhelmingly organic with only two small bolt-ons and no large M&A, and capex was committed ahead of regulatory certainty; leverage is not discussed, and four concurrent greenfields is an aggressive simultaneous commitment.
scores.quote: This project is being implemented irrespective of the final regulations, as increasing customer preference for safety will continue to drive adoption.

scores.rationale: The ABS programme has been pursued since 2021 in a segment owned by global MNCs, and management is now backward-integrating ECUs and expanding capacity ahead of final rules — a multi-year, independently financed technology push.
scores.quote: Endurance had embarked upon the ABS journey and had rolled out its first ABS in September 2021. We are the only Indian auto-ancillary Company in this domain dominated by MNC players.

scores.rationale: Calls are entirely operational — plant-by-plant SOP dates, capacities and order values — with no promotional framing or personality-led narrative.
scores.quote: Key machinery will be installed from Q1 FY 27 onwards, and the SOP is planned for Q2 FY 27.

scores.rationale: No discussion of talent development, succession or leadership pipeline appears in any of the four calls.

Disclosure is unusually granular and management strips out inorganic and tooling effects to show true organic growth and admits weak spots like KTM exports, but the repeatedly slipping dual-channel ABS SOP (next month in Aug, then Dec, then March, then June 2026) is restated without explicit acknowledgement of the delay.
scores.quote: If we remove the impact of Stöferle consolidation as well as the tooling sales, our total income grew by 7.8%.

scores.rationale: Recent outperformance is partly a GST-driven industry upcycle and Stöferle consolidation rather than pure skill, though management's own organic disclosure makes the separation possible; the greenfield ROIC thesis is still unproven.
scores.quote: the GST rate rationalization... has continued to support consumption... contributing to strong industry sales numbers well beyond the festive season

scores.rationale: Explicit leadership positions in defined niches — sole Indian player in 2W ABS, clear leader in inverted front forks and 2W/3W suspensions — give it a first-call position in the OEM's mind.
scores.quote: Endurance is by far the market leader for inverted front forks.

scores.rationale: Design-in on safety-critical parts with multi-quarter validation cycles, plus plants sited next to customers, creates real switching friction, though there is no captive aftermarket described.
scores.quote: This will help better service the South-based OEM customers and also lower our freight costs.

scores.rationale: The customer base is a handful of very large OEMs (Bajaj, TVS, Hero, Royal Enfield, Tata, Mahindra) who dictate pricing and timing — the Q4 dual-channel ABS SOP was gated on one OEM's clearance — so the end customer holds the negotiating power.
scores.quote: SOP is now expected to start next month, as we await the final clearance from a key OEM customer.

scores.rationale: ABS and BMS electronics carry real technical and validation barriers that have kept the field to MNCs plus Endurance, but OEMs are simultaneously running price and share wars downstream and Chinese entrants are pressuring Europe.
scores.quote: OEMs have targeted higher market share by way of product launches and pricing actions

scores.rationale: The localisation drive lets Endurance take ABS and casting share from higher-cost global incumbents, evidenced by Valeo and Yazaki sourcing locally and TVS/Hero switching inverted fork supply.
scores.quote: achieving first-time right parts to support the localisation drive

scores.rationale: Not an ignored niche — it is a listed mid-cap with broker-hosted quarterly calls competing in ABS against Bosch-class MNCs, though its individual product niches attract little capital.
scores.quote: hosted by Axis Capital Limited

scores.rationale: There is no image- or taste-driven pricing power; it is a component supplier passing raw material, gas and oil cost increases through to OEMs.
scores.quote: continuous monitoring of availability and cost of the raw materials, and regular interactions with customers to update them on input cost increases

scores.rationale: Products are safety-critical (brakes, ABS, battery packs) where OEMs buy validated reliability, and the company competes on first-time-right quality and compliance testing rather than price.
scores.quote: Comprehensive battery pack validation and EV safety compliance testing will be concluded during this quarter.

scores.rationale: Demonstrated customer intimacy and responsiveness — a four-month LOI-to-shipment build and ten-week sample lead time — plus deliberate plant siting next to OEM clusters.
scores.quote: completing the journey from customer LOI to facility installation in a record time of 4 months... within a record 10-week lead time

scores.rationale: Customers are corporate OEMs and the benefit set matches correctly — reliability, localisation cost savings, freight reduction and design-in lock-in rather than brand intangibles.
scores.quote: The presence of multiple global OEMs in this region enables deeper engagement

scores.rationale: A widening multi-product technology base — dual-channel ABS with traction control, in-house ECUs on its own SMT lines, BMS and battery packs — backed by two new R&D centres, though it is localising technology the global MNCs already own.
scores.quote: We are enhancing our product offering with the integration of new features such as traction control for improved stability in select applications

scores.rationale: A tier-1 component manufacturer selling into bilateral OEM contracts has no two-sided network, and nothing in the calls suggests any self-reinforcing scale dynamic.
Reach is a direct-to-OEM plant footprint rather than a distribution or service network rivals cannot replicate; proximity lowers freight but no aftermarket or service moat is described.
scores.quote: This new brakes plant will be in close proximity to certain important OEM customers.

scores.rationale: The four calls discuss order book, revenue and margins but never disclose capex, growth investment or incremental ROIC.
No mention of any advertising or promotional spend in any of the four calls.
No R&D spend, process-technology development or new-product commercialisation is discussed in the last-12-months calls.

No bolt-on M&A; the only inorganic exposure discussed is the legacy capital-heavy RFCL/Ramagundam fertilizer JV, which was shut 45 of 90 days in both Q1 and Q2 and dragged consolidated profit below standalone.
scores.quote: in this quarter also, we have loss of around INR 25 crore

scores.rationale: A coherent, consistent payout policy — Rs.2.5 interim plus Rs.2.5 final on a Rs.5 face value in FY26 — though no buyback is mentioned at all.
scores.quote: in this year we are giving 100% dividend to our shareholders

scores.rationale: Asset-light EPCM consultancy generating Rs.3,849 crores turnover with no capex programme discussed and 20-25% consultancy segment margins, but the turnkey half is a lower-return, working-capital-heavy business.
scores.quote: EIL is successful in maintaining the segment profit of 20% to 25% on the Consultancy business

scores.rationale: Order book rose from Rs.11,717 crores to Rs.15,109 crores in FY26 with materially higher overseas consultancy wins, indicating share capture outside its captive domestic base.
scores.quote: we have been able to secure around INR 1,600 crore from overseas

scores.rationale: Demonstrated international execution and wins across Abu Dhabi/Middle East, Nigeria (Dangote), Mongolia and a Rs.600+ crore Africa consultancy order, though the Q4 call flags a Middle East slowdown.
scores.quote: international has been giving good business to us, primarily from the Middle East and Abu Dhabi

scores.rationale: FY26's 27% revenue growth came from executing a record order book with mix tilting toward the low-margin turnkey segment (Rs.2,067 crores vs consultancy Rs.1,782 crores), i.e. volume-led rather than price/mix-led.
scores.quote: turnkey segment stood at Rs.2,067 crore s

scores.rationale: The company sits near a cyclical peak — all-time-high order book and record profits — with the first signs of a downturn in its overseas market rather than an upturn ahead.
scores.quote: In the Middle east part wherein we are serving there, we have seen a little bit of slowdown

scores.rationale: Domestic hydrocarbon/refinery capex is described as steady with no cancellations, but management itself calls the market dynamic and challenging rather than in permanent secular expansion.
scores.quote: we have not seen in the domestic market anywhere any project being delayed

scores.rationale: Growth is entirely organic through order wins with no acquisitions, no debt discussion and dividends funded from record cash profits, though the non-core RFCL JV remains a drag.
scores.quote: Order inflow during the Financial Year '2 5-26 stands at Rs.7,979 crore s

scores.rationale: Multi-year persistence in building overseas consultancy is evident, but as a PSU its independence is questioned even by investors on the call regarding forced JV participation.
scores.quote: What value are we getting by going in for such JVs? And is it government pressure?

scores.rationale: Calls are led by the Director-Finance and functional managers with plain numerical disclosure and no promotional or celebrity framing; the Chairman does not even appear on the calls.
scores.quote: Good afternoon, everybody, and a warm welcome to all the investors

scores.rationale: Management openly explains adverse items — JV shutdown losses, the Rs.195 crore change-order distortion, and the emerging Middle East risk — though guidance is loosely revised (20% then 25%+) and one order-inflow answer is muddled.
scores.quote: there was impact of Rs. 195 crores due to change order. That is why our quarter performance was extraordinary

scores.rationale: Record headline results are flattered by lumpy claim/change-order settlements — Q3 FY26 PBT jumped to Rs.395 crores from Rs.150 crores with 28% operating margin versus 11% — so results overstate repeatable operating skill, as an analyst directly challenged.
scores.quote: it's very difficult to model some kind of margin in both the businesses and it's quite volatile

scores.rationale: EIL is the default design/EPCM house for Indian hydrocarbon owners, repeatedly re-appointed on multi-phase mega projects such as IOCL Paradip, which reads as incumbency in the customer's mind.
scores.quote: the first phase is about to be finished... and then proceed with the second phase

scores.rationale: Phase-wise re-award on the same asset and a Rs.7,500 crore consultancy backlog from a narrow set of domestic refiners evidence real switching costs and captive follow-on work.
scores.quote: under Consultancy segment of INR7,500 crores

scores.rationale: Domestic hydrocarbon consultancy shows oligopolistic economics with sustained 20-25% segment margins and repeat inflow near Rs.8,000 crores for two consecutive years, though clients are large PSU buyers with real bargaining power.
scores.quote: we have 2 years we have consistently maintained

scores.rationale: Consultancy pricing is rational and stable at 20-25%, but the turnkey/LSTK half earns only 6-7%, indicating a low-barrier, competitively bid business alongside the protected one.
scores.quote: in the LSTK, we will maintain 6 % to 7% segment profit

scores.rationale: The calls never identify competitors or discuss weak players from whom share could be taken.
It is a niche engineering consultancy but is a listed PSU covered by DAM Capital, ICICI Securities, PL Capital and Nirmal Bang, so it is not ignored by capital.
scores.quote: the line of Manish Ostwal from Nirmal Bang Securities

scores.rationale: There is no image- or taste-driven pricing power; profitability rests on technical scope, and the blended operating margin of 16.22% with volatile quarterly swings shows limited pricing insulation.
scores.quote: Operating margin during the Financial Year '2 5-26 increased to 16.22%

scores.rationale: Clients award multi-thousand-crore, safety-critical refinery mandates on track record rather than price, evidenced by a Rs.3,250 crore single January order and repeated re-engagement.
scores.quote: in January 2026, the company has bagged an order of around INR3,250 crores

scores.rationale: Local presence and general services in the Middle East plus a dedicated marketing/BD function are referenced, but there is no evidence of distinctive accessibility versus rivals.
scores.quote: we have general services

scores.rationale: The customer base is entirely corporate/PSU buying reliability and lifecycle project certainty, with lock-in via phased project incumbency — the correct benefit match for that customer type.
scores.quote: IOCL Parad ip, I think there was a large order

scores.rationale: No discussion of proprietary process technology, licensing income or R&D intensity in any of the four calls.
Nothing in the calls bears on two-sided or self-reinforcing network dynamics.

The firm executes across India, Africa, the Middle East and Mongolia, but overseas consultancy revenue actually fell to a Rs.70-75 crore quarterly run rate, so reach is not demonstrably superior to rivals.
scores.quote: now this year, it is about INR 70 crore to INR 75 crore quarterly run rate

scores.rationale: Three announced expansions are pure growth capex — Kalwa transformer capacity doubling and Sambhajinagar switchgear (₹7.4bn) plus a new ₹20.6bn greenfield transformer plant — landing into a 22% backlog growth and rising margins, implying strong incremental returns.
scores.quote: Two of them are brownfield expansions of ₹7.4 billion... doubling the capacity from 15,000 to 30,000 MVA... the new one... is ₹20.6 billion, where we will implement a new greenfield transformer factory

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend in either call.

Four engineering/R&D centres and ~1,500 engineers plugged into the global R&D network with an IIT Bombay MoU and differentiated outputs (PEM electrolyzers, SF6-free clean-air switchgear), but the core product IP is the parent's and no local R&D-to-revenue efficiency is quantified.
